items.title: 4 Killed in Ukrainian Attack on Novorossiysk
items.summary: Russian officials said more than two dozen people were wounded during the overnight attack on the port city.
items.body_text:
Four people including a child were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack in the southern Krasnodar region, local officials said Wednesday.
Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said another 29 people were wounded in the attack, which took place in Novorossiysk, a frequent target of Ukrainian drone strikes and a major outlet for Russian oil, petroleum products and grain exports.
Novorossiysk Mayor Andrei Kravchenko said drone debris fell on the premises of a number of businesses and close to a residential building.
In Anapa, another town in the Krasnodar region, three homes and a kindergarten were damaged by falling drone debris, but no one was injured, Kondratyev said.
Russia's Defense Ministry said it intercepted 596 Ukrainian drones across Russia and annexed Crimea between Tuesday night and Wednesday morning.
Airports in more than a dozen regions introduced temporary flight restrictions amid the cross-country drone attacks.
Meanwhile, in Ukraine, a Russian drone attack on a border crossing with neighboring Moldova killed two people and injured at least three others.
Passenger and vehicle traffic was temporarily halted across the border after the attack, which caused a major fire, officials said.
Reuters contributed reporting.

items.title: 22-year-old Russian conscript sent to war despite suicide attempt. He went missing after an assault operation and was later declared dead.
items.summary: Alexander Korolkov, a 22-year-old conscript from Dmitrov, outside Moscow, was sent to fight in the war with Ukraine despite having attempted suicide during his military service, Veter reported after interviewing his mother.
items.body_text:
22-year-old Russian conscript sent to war despite suicide attempt. He went missing after an assault operation and was later declared dead.
Alexander Korolkov, a 22-year-old conscript from Dmitrov, outside Moscow, was sent to fight in the war with Ukraine despite having attempted suicide during his military service, Veter reported after interviewing his mother.
Korolkov had been studying to become a food technologist at a vocational college when, in the summer of 2024, he took academic leave — and immediately received a summons from the local draft office. He was sent to serve, and a month later doctors diagnosed him with “mixed personality disorder.” At a training center for engineering troops in the Nizhny Novgorod region, he attempted to take his own life.
“I think it’s all because of the army, because Sasha is very kind, trusting, and sensitive. We didn’t have any problems like teenagers sometimes have, with partying or anything like that. He’s a very homebound boy. There, it seems, he couldn’t handle the pressure,” Maria Korolkova, the conscript’s mother, said.
After the training center, Korolkov was sent to a military unit in the town of Boguchar, in the Voronezh region, his mother said. There, he was admitted to a psychoneurological clinic and prescribed medication. She was assured he would not be deployed. But five days after his discharge from the clinic, Korolkov signed a contract for military service in Ukraine.
“We told Sasha that he absolutely should not sign a contract. Then he called me and said they had pushed him into it,” his mother said. The military unit refused to show her the contract, and she believes it was fabricated.
In April 2025, Korolkov’s unit sent him on an assault operation in the occupied territories of Ukraine. He went missing there, and in the summer of 2026, the unit petitioned a court to have him declared dead. His mother received a death certificate for her son.

items.title: Russia’s trade ministry says not all marketplace warehouses damaged in Ukrainian drone strikes need to be rebuilt
items.summary: Russian authorities and marketplace operators plan to decide by the end of 2026 whether every logistics complex damaged in Ukrainian drone strikes needs to be rebuilt, the Russian state news agency TASS reported.
items.body_text:
Russia’s trade ministry says not all marketplace warehouses damaged in Ukrainian drone strikes need to be rebuilt
Russian authorities and marketplace operators plan to decide by the end of 2026 whether every logistics complex damaged in Ukrainian drone strikes needs to be rebuilt, the Russian state news agency TASS reported.
It’s still too early to say that a full “hundred percent restoration of exactly the same logistics centers that existed” is needed, said Roman Chekushov, deputy head of the Industry and Trade Ministry:
By the end of the year, we will understand how logistics will be restructured, what the scope of the damage is, and whether government involvement in the rebuilding will be needed. If any restoration of certain logistics capacities will be needed at all.
Ukraine has repeatedly attacked Wildberries’s largest warehouses across Russia with drones since mid-June. Drones later began striking warehouses belonging to another marketplace, Ozon.
By early August, the damage to Wildberries and its sellers from the drone strikes was estimated at hundreds of billions of rubles.
In late August, Russia’s government approved support measures — including a tax deferral — for both the Wildberries sellers affected by the warehouse strikes and the marketplace itself.

items.body_text:
‘Kyiv is gasping for breath’: Russia’s escalating attacks are upending daily life in the Ukrainian capital. Here’s how residents are coping.
Russian attacks on Kyiv and the surrounding region intensified in late spring, and since August 27, the only respite has come during a visit to the Ukrainian capital by U.S. presidential envoys. Kyiv residents were able to go a full day without air raid alerts only on September 6. The shift in Russian strike tactics is linked to the Russian army’s effort to exhaust Ukraine’s air defenses. In addition to military warehouses, civilian facilities have also come under attack. One of the new targets has been warehouses in the Kyiv region — likely struck in retaliation for the Ukrainian military’s summer strikes on Ozon and Wildberries warehouses and oil refineries. Daytime air raid alerts paralyze life in the city, while nighttime alerts interrupt the sleep of hundreds of thousands of people. Disrupted logistics have caused some goods to disappear from Kyiv supermarkets. Meduza spoke with Kyiv residents who are trying to live amid constant shelling — and are already preparing for a harsh winter.
‘We saw a fireball that looked like an exploding sun’
Marusya, 42, lives in Borshchahivka
No one in Kyiv sleeps normally these days — except for those on some kind of heavy medication. I take sleeping pills every so often, when it gets unbearable and I just want to get some sleep.
We’ve gotten used to nighttime shelling, but lately they’ve started shelling us during the day too — that’s something new. Along with the familiar buzzing, droning, and explosions, there are now sounds that put you on edge simply because they’re unfamiliar. A kind of rumble with a metallic, almost “galvanized” overtone.
Waking up to an explosion at night is scary: you’re defenseless and relaxed. During the day you keep yourself alert — so something went boom, fine. But the daytime alerts have become nonstop. I didn’t think it would drag on this long. It seemed like there’d be some banging and then it would calm down, but the lull never comes.
I don’t think this is retaliation for the strikes on Wildberries. And even if it is, it’s just a pretext. If there hadn’t been such a pretext, they would have tied it to something else. They’ve probably been stockpiling and gathering up [missiles]. If there’s an urge to pound, they’ll pound regardless.
Overnight on August 21, a friend of mine in Solomianka had a strike hit the building next door. She got lucky: the day before, she and her son had ended up staying over at someone else’s place for the night. The blast blew out the windows in her apartment, knocked the doors off their hinges, and brought down her half-condemned balcony. My friend jokes, “I was already afraid it would fall on someone’s head. Thank God the blast wave tore it off.”
There are plenty of damaged buildings in our neighborhood too [because of the war]: you look around and there’s a chunk missing from one building here, another there. I checked on my map app: the nearest building hit by a major strike is 800 meters (2,625 feet) from mine.
There’s a shelter in the building next door, but I haven’t even gone down there out of curiosity. I don’t see the point. If the building collapses, it’s harder to pull bodies out of a shelter than out of a bed. I don’t understand people who still believe in the “two walls” rule and hang out in hallways. I think if it’s going to hit, it’s going to hit. I especially crack up when I hear on the tram: “The nearest shelter is the underground crossing.” Have you seen that underground crossing in Lukianivka? What kind of “shelter” is that?!
Over the entire course of the full-scale war, my husband and I have left our apartment [for safety] only twice. The first time was at the start of the invasion, and the second was recently, when a Zircon missile was launched at Kyiv. items.title: Philippines defence chief gets China's note mid-speech; his blunt reply stuns room
items.body_text:
NEW DELHI: Philippines defence secretary Gilberto C Teodoro publicly rebuked China at a defence forum in Seoul after a note outlining Beijing's position on the South China Sea arbitration was handed to him while he was speaking.
Teodoro was addressing maritime challenges and the South China Sea at the Seoul Defence Dialogue when a man approached him from behind and placed a sheet of paper on the table. Teodoro paused, picked up the note and asked whether it had come from China before reading parts of it aloud. "I have a note here. I think this is from China. And may I read it?" he said.
As Teodoro read the note, he interrupted its argument with a blunt response: "They have no position." The note stated that China's position on the South China Sea arbitration was "clear, consistent and firm" and argued that the arbitration violated fundamental principles of international law.
Teodoro then challenged the legal argument contained in the note, referring to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), under which the Philippines had brought the arbitration case against China. "So what you signed unclause. 
You mean violates international law. That's what you mean," he said.
The note further described the arbitration ruling as illegal, null and void and said it had no binding force. The 2016 arbitration tribunal rejected China's expansive historic-rights claims in the South China Sea and found no legal basis for Beijing's claims to resources within the Philippines' exclusive economic zone. China has rejected the ruling and maintained that the tribunal had no jurisdiction.
The Philippine defence chief then turned the incident into a broader criticism of Beijing's conduct, questioning the decision to deliver the message while he was addressing an international audience.
"How can you deal with a country in an international forum beyond the question asked to me disrespecting the organizers of this forum, how do you expect to deal with it civilly?" Teodoro said.
He argued that the episode went beyond the legal dispute and amounted to a lack of respect for the forum's organisers and South Korea, which was hosting the event.
"If this is a Chinese position sent to me, it not only disrespects international law throwing uncloths to the floor and trampling upon it, but it also disrespects the basic decency accorded that should be accorded to our most gracious hosts, the Republic of Korea and the rest of the audience here," he said.
Teodoro then accused China of using pressure against the Philippines, saying, "Perhaps basic decency and behavior is what China needs to do now."
He said he would retain the note as a reminder of what he described as Beijing's weakness in making its case.
"I will keep this paper as a memento of how desperate China is and how ineffective its position is in the face of a free audience," Teodoro said.
He also directed a sarcastic remark at the person who had handed over the note, saying, "You just done your country a great service. Thank you. And I hope you don't suffer in a gulag for it."
What initially appeared to be a deliberate interruption was later reported to have resulted from a mix-up.
According to forum organisers, the note had been sent by a Chinese military attache with the Chinese Embassy in Seoul, Yonhap News Agency reported. The attache reportedly handed it to a forum staff member with instructions that it be passed to Teodoro.
The staff member apparently mistook it for a message from Teodoro's own delegation and handed it to him while he was speaking.
Teodoro targets China's South China Sea claims
Teodoro used the episode to reiterate Manila's concerns over China's activities in the South China Sea, particularly in areas that the Philippines considers part of its exclusive economic zone.

items.title: Father-in-law must 'quit politics': Mayawati's condition for Akash's big role
items.summary: BSP chief Mayawati stated Ashok Siddharth must retire from politics for Akash Anand's return. Akash Anand was removed from national convener and needs more maturity. The party will consider Akash Anand's responsibilities after Siddharth's complete political exit. Mayawati also readmitted expelled leaders and hinted at Ishan Anand's new party role. These developments precede upcoming assembly elections in Punjab and Uttar Pradesh.
items.body_text:
LUCKNOW: 
BSP
 national president 
Mayawati
 said on Tuesday that Ashok Siddharth, the father-in-law of her nephew Akash Anand, should take complete "sanyas" from politics. Only then, she said, would it be appropriate for Akash Anand to work freely in the party again.
Akash Anand was the BSP's national convener until September 3, when Mayawati announced at an all-India meeting of party office-bearers that he would work as an ordinary party worker. She said it would not be appropriate to give him any major responsibility, adding that he still needed to become more "mature."
Mayawati said on Tuesday that the party leadership will consider giving Akash Anand's responsibilities back to him only after Ashok Siddharth gives up politics completely.
Ashok Siddharth, a former Rajya Sabha MP of the party, was expelled by Mayawati on August 2 for alleged anti-party activities.
What happened on September 3
At the September 3 meeting, Mayawati told BSP office-bearers: "I have allowed Akash Anand to work in the party, which is before all of you, but Akash Anand still needs to become more mature. Till then, it would not be appropriate to give him a major responsibility in the party."
She said Akash Anand, as national coordinator, would continue to work in the party. Mayawati invoked BSP founder Kanshi Ram's approach of allowing family members to assist with party work but opposing giving them election tickets or positions after the party came to power. "I am also completely committed to that resolve," she said.
At the same meeting, Mayawati announced that the BSP has decided to contest all elections across the country on its own, without alliances. She also described the Congress as "strongly anti-Dalit and anti-Ambedkar" and criticised the RSS, citing recent remarks by its chief Mohan Bhagwat during his US visit.
Both Akash Anand and Ishan Anand, Mayawati's younger nephew, attended the September 3 meeting.
The reshuffle around him
In the same period, Mayawati has brought back several previously expelled leaders into the party fold.
Former national coordinator Randhir Singh Beniwal, expelled in August for alleged anti-party activities and indiscipline, has rejoined the BSP and been assigned as central coordinator responsible for organising the party in selected states. Senior leader Ashok Siddharth was removed at the same time as Beniwal but remains outside the party.
Dharamveer Ashok, a former minister in the Mayawati-led UP government in 2007 and a former member of the legislative council, was expelled in April on similar charges and was readmitted in August.
Meerut-based leaders Mohit Anand and Nitin Singh have also been named central coordinators. Singh was expelled last year and reinstated a few months later.
Party sources said Mayawati is expanding the BSP's organisation at the national and state levels, with several returning leaders appointed as central coordinators to build cadres, oversee outreach, and strengthen the party's footprint in their allotted states.
Ishan Anand may get his first party role
Mayawati has also dropped hints that she may appoint Ishan Anand, her younger nephew, as in charge of Sector-1 and Sector-2 in the party organisation, according to sources aware of a late-night meeting of national-level office-bearers held at her residence. No official announcement has been made.
Sector-1 and Sector-2 cover all state units except Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand, which remain under Mayawati's direct supervision. If confirmed, the role would be Ishan Anand's first formal responsibility in the BSP.
Ishan Anand, 27, is a graduate in legal studies from the University of Westminster in the UK. He made his first public appearance on the party stage on January 15, 2025, during Mayawati's birthday event, and attended a state-level meeting of the BSP's UP unit the next day â seen at the time as a signal of his growing involvement ahead of the 2027 assembly elections.

items.title: 5 ‘lost’ baby orangutans found in Odisha forest
items.summary: Five juvenile orangutans were discovered abandoned in a forest in Odisha's Balasore district. Forest officials suspect a transoceanic trafficking network smuggled the young apes into India. Villagers alerted the forest department after spotting the orangutans dangling from tree branches. The animals were safely secured without the use of tranquilizers by forest personnel. A Wildlife Crime Control Bureau team is investigating the origin of these exotic animals.
items.body_text:
BHUBANESWAR: Five juvenile orangutans, native to Southeast Asia and never recorded in the wild anywhere in India, were found abandoned Tuesday morning in a casuarina forest off NH-16 in 
Odisha
âs Balasore district.
Forest officials suspect a transoceanic trafficking network smuggled the apes, all less than a year old, into India and abandoned them near Badipada, in Chandaneswar, after realising they might be caught.
Villagers spotted the orangutans dangling from tree branches inside the Bhogarai forest, about 40 km from the Balasore-Kolkata stretch of NH-16, and alerted the forest department.
âOur field personnel visited the site and were surprised to discover that all five were baby orangutans, two of them females. As a crowd started gathering near the forest, we decided to bring a cage and safely secure the animals without using tranquillisers,â Balasore divisional forest officer Prateek Indalkar said.
âThe orangutans were extremely calm. Our team picked up the animals and placed them inside the cage without any difficulty.â
Indalkar said the animals might have been transported by road from Kolkata. âSince orangutans are not available in India, we suspect they came from Malaysia to Kolkata by ship.
The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) has the expertise to determine the exact species and identify the country from which they originated.â
Chief wildlife warden Prem Kumar Jha said orangutans are easy prey for traffickers and are kept illegally as exotic pets by wealthy collectors in several countries.
âWhether the animals were being taken to Kolkata for sale to affluent buyers or being moved to another destination will be established soon,â he said.
A WCCB team is travelling to Balasore to investigate the animalsâ origin. State forest minister Ganesh Ram Singhkhuntia said the probe would go into âhow the animals landed in Balasore and from where they were brought since they are not available in India in their natural habitatâ.
After a medical examination, the rescued orangutans were shifted to the animal rescue centre at Bhubaneswarâs Nandankanan Zoological Park.

items.title: Thailand reduces visa-free stay for Indians from 60 to 30 days
items.summary: The new rules will replace the visa exemption scheme from 2024, which allowed sixty days of visa-free stay for Indians in Thailand
items.body_text:
Thailand has introduced new rules for tourists from over 60 countries, including for Indian passport holders. The Royal Gazette of Thailand published the new rules on August 31, 2026. The new rules will replace the 60-day visa exemption scheme from 2024, which allowed sixty days of visa-free stay for Indians.
Under Thailand’s current tourist scheme, travellers from more than 90 countries, including Europe’s 29-nation Schengen area, China, India, the United States and several South American countries, are eligible to visit for up to 60 days without a visa. The new regulations will come into effect from September 15, 2026.
What does this mean for Indian tourists?
Indian passport holders will be able to enter Thailand without obtaining a visa in advance for tourism, but their permitted visa-free stay will now be reduced from sixty to thirty days under the new rules.
Why is Thailand changing the rules?
As reported by news outlet AFP, a string of recent arrests has included foreigners accused of drug offences, sex trafficking, and operating businesses such as hotels and schools without proper permits. It quotes Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow, who had said in May that the plan to trim visa-free visits was part of a crackdown on individuals abusing the visa system by committing crimes in the country.
Which countries are affected by the new Thai rules?
The 60 countries and territories eligible for the thirty-day visa exemption are Australia, Austria, Bahrain, Belgium, Bulgaria, Bhutan, Brunei, Canada, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Fiji, Finland, France, Georgia, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Indonesia, India, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Jordan, Kuwait, Kyrgyzstan, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Malaysia, Maldives, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Oman, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Qatar, Romania, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Slovakia, Slovenia, South Africa, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Türkiye, Ukraine, United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom, and the United States, according to the notification in The Royal Gazette, signed by Thailand PM and Minister of Interior Anutin Charnvirakul.

items.title: Suspected measles cases kill nearly 1,000 as Bangladesh struggles to contain outbreak
items.summary: Bangladesh has been racing to halt the outbreak's spread since March, when more than 100 children died in less than a month
items.body_text:
Eight-month-old Rojatun Jannat Ramisa is struggling to breathe in a hospital in Bangladesh’s capital as her parents sit helplessly beside her. She's one of thousands of children sickened by a measles outbreak that's sweeping across the country and has killed hundreds of children following setbacks to the country's vaccine programme.
Ramisa’s mother Ranu Akhter travelled hundreds of kilometres after doctors in eastern Bangladesh referred her to a specialised child hospital in Dhaka to seek treatment for the life-threatening condition.
“Fourteen days ago, when we were at the district hospital, there were other children being treated alongside my daughter. I saw that those children also had red rashes on their bodies, sores in their mouths and fevers,” Ms. Akhter told The Associated Press at Dhaka Shishu Hospital.
“It made me realise how widespread the measles outbreak is,” she said. Every day, the death toll is rising.
Bangladesh has been racing to halt the outbreak's spread since March, when more than 100 children died in less than a month. By Tuesday (September 8, 2026), the death toll from suspected measles cases reached 999 since the start of the year, according to the government’s Directorate General of Health Services.
Since March, the country has recorded more than 1,66,000 suspected measles cases, including 19,835 laboratory-confirmed infections, according to the Ministry of Health.
The government launched an emergency vaccination drive in March together with the World Health Organization, the U.N. children’s agency and the Gavi vaccine alliance. It began with a focus on children from six months to five years old and later expanded nationwide in phases.
Measles is a highly contagious airborne disease that causes fever, respiratory symptoms and a characteristic rash. It can sometimes have severe or fatal complications, especially in young children, according to the WHO.
Two doses of a vaccine provide strong protection against measles, but the WHO says 95% of the population has to be vaccinated in order to stop the disease from spreading — which protects children like Ramisa who are too young to be vaccinated as well as immunocompromised people.
A few years ago, Bangladesh, had measles largely under control, with a vaccination programme that was credited for decades for protecting children and mothers from the deadly diseases of tuberculosis, diphtheria, whooping cough, tetanus, poliomyelitis and measles. Between 2021 and 2025, the country recorded just 100 to 300 cases per year, down from 2,410 cases in 2020.
But in the last few years, disruptions to the vaccine programme have left a growing number of children unvaccinated.
First the pandemic interrupted routine vaccinations, and then in 2024 the government largely missed a vaccination campaign previously carried out every four years.
Atiqul Islam, a neonatal and child specialist at Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute, said during the pandemic period in 2021 and 2022, many did not take their children to get vaccinated.
“So, if you look at children who are now four or five years old, many of them missed their vaccinations. That created a gap. During the previous interim government, vaccines were also unavailable at many vaccination centers,” he said.
Bangladesh's current government, headed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, said the failures in planning under ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and interim leader Muhammad Yunus left the country with shortages of vaccines and far behind on coverage.
The 2024 measles vaccination campaign was disrupted during the political upheaval that led to Hasina’s ouster. She left the country in the face of a mass uprising in August 2024, and was followed by Mr. Yunus, who led an interim administration that transferred power to an elected government after an election in February.
From exile in India, Ms. Hasina blamed the Yunus-led government for the disaster. At Bangladesh Shishu Hospital, Mr. Islam said the situation has improved,

items.title: U.S. suspends Cognizant’s green-card filings; IT industry may face tougher scrutiny
items.summary: Labour Department action amid alleged fraud probe puts new PERM filings on hold; experts say technology companies could face greater scrutiny of visa sponsorship, recruitment, wages and compliance
items.body_text:
The U.S. Department of Labour has suspended Cognizant Technology Solutions’ filings under the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme, a key step for employers seeking employment-based green cards for foreign workers, amid an investigation into alleged fraud.
“Cognizant’s PERM filings are suspended,” U.S. Labour Department Inspector General Anthony D’Esposito announced on X, adding that the department was working with the White House Task Force to eliminate fraud. “Threats to American workers will NOT be tolerated,” he added.
The department has not disclosed the specific allegations against Cognizant, the number of filings affected or how long the suspension will remain in force. The material released by the inspector general also does not identify any criminal charges against Cognizant.
PERM is the labour-certification stage of the employment-based permanent residency process. Under the programme, the Labour Department must certify that qualified U.S. workers are not available for a position and that hiring a foreign worker will not adversely affect the wages and working conditions of similarly employed American workers.
EIITREND CEO Pareekh Jain said a prolonged suspension could create a talent-retention risk for Cognizant if it affects employees already in the green-card queue.
He said employees could consider moving to other companies if their permanent-residency process remains stalled, making it a potential medium-term issue for Cognizant.
Mr. Jain said the impact could be broader if similar action is taken against other technology companies, potentially pushing the industry towards more local hiring. He also said the significance of the move was that immigration scrutiny could now extend beyond H-1B hiring to the H-1B-to-green-card pathway.
He also questioned why Cognizant was the first pick, noting that although it was founded in Chennai, it is a U.S.-headquartered and Nasdaq-listed company. He said this suggested the move is intended to be less about an India-U.S. issue and more about sending a signal to the wider IT industry, although the U.S. government has not stated this as its rationale.
In his Linkedin post, Piyal Gupta, CEO of Kneuralabs and a former Accenture and Cognizant executive, said the suspension was significant for the global IT industry because PERM is a critical step in the employment-based green-card process.
Mr. Gupta said the development should be watched closely by Indian technology professionals who depend on employer-sponsored green cards, but cautioned against treating an investigation as proof that Cognizant committed fraud.
He said the broader implication for the industry could be greater scrutiny of immigration-related compliance, including wages, recruitment practices and documentation.
“The era of treating H-1B and Green Card sponsorship simply as an HR process is changing,” he said, adding that companies could face greater scrutiny around compliance.
The development came a day after Cognizant announced that it planned to hire 1,500 US college graduates and scale its combined Frontier Certified Engineer and Frontier Business Operator workforce to 15,000.
In a September 7 announcement, Cognizant CEO Ravi Kumar S. said, “We are hiring American graduates, standing up new American job categories for the AI era, and putting Cognizant’s capital and leadership behind a national coalition built to make sure this transition works for workers.”

भारत रत्न वैज्ञानिक सीएनआर राव को नोटिस:नाम में Prof की जगह Proff लिखा; SIR के दौरान कई हस्तियों के साथ हो चुके विवाद
- कॉपी लिंक
कर्नाटक में स्पेशल इंटेंसिव रिवीजन (SIR) के बाद भारत रत्न वैज्ञानिक सीएनआर राव को नाम में गड़बड़ी के मामले में नोटिस जारी किया गया है। पुराने रिकॉर्ड में उनका नाम ‘ProfCNR राव’ है, जबकि नए रिकॉर्ड में ‘Proff CNR राव’ लिखा है।
नोटिस में उन्हें इस मामले को सुलझाने के लिए बेंगलुरु के मल्लेश्वरम में सुनवाई के लिए पेश होने को कहा गया है। हालांकि, राव के कार्यालय ने कहा कि उन्हें अब तक कोई नोटिस नहीं मिला है। नोटिस ऑनलाइन जारी किया गया है, लेकिन उन्होंने इसे देखा नहीं है। राव को 2014 में भारत रत्न से सम्मानित किया जा चुका है।
कर्नाटक में SIR 17 अगस्त को खत्म हुआ। इसके बाद 23 सितंबर तक आपत्तियां और नोटिस पर चुनाव आयाोग में सुनवाई चलेगी। SIR के दौरान कई हस्तियों के साथ हो चुके विवाद। इनमें राहुल द्रविड़, प्रकाश राज और राघव चड्ढा का भी नाम शामिल है।
राहुल द्रविड़ और राघव चड्ढा समेत कई के नाम कटने पर विवाद
राहुल द्रविड़- घर बदलने के बाद पुराने पते से नाम कट गया, नए पते पर ट्रांसफर नहीं हुआ।
प्रकाश राज- पते के वेरिफिकेशन के दौरान 'शिफ्टेड' (स्थानांतरित) मानकर लिस्ट से नाम हटा दिया गया।
राम जेठमलानी- रोल अपडेशन की तकनीकी खामी के कारण नाम डिलीट हो गया।
राघव चड्ढा- वोटर लिस्ट रिवीजन के दौरान पते के वेरिफिकेशन पर तकनीकी आपत्ति दर्ज हुई।
CNR राव का वैज्ञानिक करियर
CNR राव का जन्म 1934 में बेंगलुरु में हुआ था। उन्होंने केमिस्ट्री रिसर्च में योगदान दिया है। इनमें सॉलिड-स्टेट मैटेरियल्स, नैनोमैटेरियल्स और स्ट्रक्चरल केमिस्ट्री शामिल हैं।
उन्होंने 1976 में IISc में सॉलिड स्टेट एंड स्ट्रक्चरल केमिस्ट्री यूनिट की स्थापना की थी। वे 1984 से 1994 तक IISc के निदेशक रहे।
सीएनआर राव ने 1,600 से ज्यादा रिसर्च पेपर लिखे हैं और उन्हें कई अंतरराष्ट्रीय सम्मानों से सम्मानित किया जा चुका है।
दिल्ली, महाराष्ट्र समेत 16 राज्यों में SIR का तीसरा फेज
चुनाव आयोग ने 14 मई को हरियाणा, झारखंड, उत्तराखंड, दिल्ली और महाराष्ट्र समेत 16 राज्यों और 3 केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में स्पेशल इंटेसिव रिवीजन (SIR) की घोषणा की थी। यह SIR का तीसरा फेज है।
पूरी प्रक्रिया 30 मई से 23 दिसंबर तक चलेगी। इस दौरान 36.73 करोड़ वोटरों का वेरिफिकेशन हो रहा है। जिन राज्यों में SIR होगा, उनमें पंजाब, उत्तराखंड और मणिपुर में अगले साल विधानसभा चुनाव हैं। अन्य 13 राज्यों में 2028 और 2029 में चुनाव होंगे।
10 राज्यों और 3 केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में पूरा हुआ SIR
SIR के पहले और दूसरे फेज में 10 राज्य और 3 केंद्र शासित प्रदेश कवर हो चुके हैं। SIR के बाद बिहार, पश्चिम बंगाल, पुडुचेरी और असम विधानसभा चुनाव में भाजपा जीती है। केरल में कांग्रेस गठबंधन और तमिलनाडु में TVK ने जीत हासिल की है। असम में स्पेशल रिवीजन (SR) हुआ। यहां भी भाजपा सरकार की वापसी हुई।

items.summary: श्रीनगर में मुख्यमंत्री उमर अब्दुल्ला और जम्मू-कश्मीर नेशनल कॉन्फ्रेंस अध्यक्ष फारूक अब्दुल्ला की मौजूदगी में पूरा वंदे मातरम गाए जाने पर कांग्रेस ने आपत्ति जताई है। इस पर उमर की पार्टी नेशनल कॉन्फ्रेंस ने कहा कि गठबंधन के सहयोगियों पर शर्तें थोपने का अधिकार कांग्रेस का नहीं है। वहीं, बीजेपी ने कांग्रेस को ‘मुस्लिम लीग’ की राजनीति करने वाली पार्टी बताया। विवाद सोमवार को जम्मू-कश्मीर के अंतरराष्ट्रीय फिल्म महोत्सव में राष्ट्रीय गीत का पूरा संस्करण गाए जाने के बाद शुरू हुआ। कांग्रेस के संगठन महासच

- Hindi News
- National
- Srinagar Film Festival Vande Mataram Controversy | Omar Abdullah & BJP
जम्मू-कश्मीर के सीएम उमर ने पूरा वंदे मातरम गाया:कांग्रेस ने आपत्ति जताई, कहा- सहयोगी दल पार्टी के साथ रहे; बीजेपी ने कांग्रेस को नई मुस्लिम लीग बताया
- कॉपी लिंक
श्रीनगर में मुख्यमंत्री उमर अब्दुल्ला और जम्मू-कश्मीर नेशनल कॉन्फ्रेंस अध्यक्ष फारूक अब्दुल्ला की मौजूदगी में पूरा वंदे मातरम गाए जाने पर कांग्रेस ने आपत्ति जताई है।
इस पर उमर की पार्टी नेशनल कॉन्फ्रेंस ने कहा कि गठबंधन के सहयोगियों पर शर्तें थोपने का अधिकार कांग्रेस का नहीं है। वहीं, बीजेपी ने कांग्रेस को ‘मुस्लिम लीग’ की राजनीति करने वाली पार्टी बताया।
विवाद सोमवार को जम्मू-कश्मीर के अंतरराष्ट्रीय फिल्म महोत्सव में राष्ट्रीय गीत का पूरा संस्करण गाए जाने के बाद शुरू हुआ।
कांग्रेस के संगठन महासचिव केसी वेणुगोपाल ने कार्यक्रम का वीडियो शेयर करते नेशनल कॉन्फ्रेंस से अपील की कि वह कांग्रेस के साथ खड़ी रहे और वंदे मातरम के 2 पैरा गाने के पक्ष में अपना रुख कायम रखे।
नेशनल कॉन्फ्रेंस बोली- वंदे मातरम गाना या कितना गाना है, यह लोगों की पसंद
नेशनल कॉन्फ्रेंस के नेता बशीर अहमद ने कहा कि गठबंधन सहयोगी होने के नाते कांग्रेस यह तय नहीं कर सकती कि वंदे मातरम गाना है या कितना गाना है।
उन्होंने कहा कि वेणुगोपाल को ट्वीट करने का अधिकार है, लेकिन वह अपना फैसला थोप नहीं सकते। यह लोगों की पसंद का मामला है और उनकी पार्टी किसी पर कुछ थोपने के खिलाफ है।
वेणुगोपाल ने कहा कि वंदे मातरम के उसी संस्करण को गाया जाना चाहिए, जिसे उस समय अपनाया गया था। इस संस्करण को जानबूझकर इसलिए चुना गया था, ताकि गीत को सांप्रदायिक रंग देने से बचाया जा सके।
कांग्रेस ने तय किया था- वंदे मातरम के दो पैरा गाए जाएंगे
कांग्रेस वर्किंग कमेटी ने ऐलान किया था कि पार्टी अपने सभी कार्यक्रमों में वंदे मातरम के 6 में से सिर्फ शुरुआती दो पैरा गाएगी। यह फैसला 15 अगस्त को कांग्रेस मुख्यालय में वंदे मातरम के गायन को लेकर हुए विवाद के बाद आया।
कांग्रेस का यह फैसला बीजेपी के उन आरोपों के बाद आया था, जिसमें बीजेपी ने कांग्रेस नेताओं पर पार्टी कार्यक्रमों में वंदे मातरम का पूरा संस्करण नहीं गाकर उसका अपमान करने का आरोप लगाया था।
2026 वंदे मातरम के अपमान पर कानून बना
- 24 जनवरी 1950 को संविधान सभा ने 'वंदे मातरम' को राष्ट्रीय गीत घोषित किया था। लंबे समय तक इसके अपमान पर कोई अलग कानून नहीं था, लेकिन 2026 के मानसून सत्र में केंद्र सरकार ने 'राष्ट्रीय गौरव अपमान निवारण अधिनियम' बनाया।
- इस कानून के तहत 'वंदे मातरम' के गायन को जानबूझकर रोकने, इसमें बाधा डालने या इसका सार्वजनिक अपमान करने को दंडनीय अपराध माना गया है। ऐसा करने पर 3 साल तक की जेल, जुर्माना या दोनों की सजा का प्रावधान है।
- इस बार 15 अगस्त को स्वतंत्रता दिवस समारोह के दौरान पहली बार लाल किले की प्राचीर से 'वंदे मातरम्' के पूरे 6 छंद गाए गए।
केंद्र का आदेश- पहले वंदे मातरम, फिर जन गण मन होगा
गृह मंत्रालय ने 9 जुलाई को सभी राज्यों, केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों और केंद्रीय मंत्रालयों को राष्ट्रीय गीत ‘वंदे मातरम’ और राष्ट्रगान ‘जन गण मन’ के गायन और बजाने को लेकर नए निर्देश जारी किए थे। इसमें दोनों के सही बोल, उच्चारण और तय प्रोटोकॉल का पालन करने को कहा गया था।
निर्देशों के मुताबिक, अगर किसी कार्यक्रम में वंदे मातरम और जन गण मन दोनों गाए या बजाए जाते हैं, तो पहले वंदे मातरम और उसके बाद राष्ट्रगान होगा। अगर किसी राज्य या केंद्र शासित प्रदेश का अपना राज्य गीत भी है, तो पहले राज्य गीत फिर वंदे मातरम और अंत में जन गण मन रहेगा।
---------------
ये खबर भी पढ़ें…
कांग्रेस वंदे मातरम के दो ही पैरा गाएगी:1937 के फैसले का पालन करेगी, वेणुगोपाल बोले- भाजपा के लिए ये भावनात्मक नहीं, राजनीति मुद्दा
कांग्रेस ने वंदे मातरम को लेकर अपना रुख साफ कर दिया है। कांग्रेस महासचिव केसी वेणुगोपाल ने कहा कि पार्टी 1937 में हुई कांग्रेस बैठक में लिए गए फैसले का पालन करेगी। इसके तहत पार्टी के कार्यक्रमों में वंदे मातरम के केवल दो अंतरे गाए जाएंगे। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
- भास्कर एक्सक्लूसिवCM ने जॉइनिंग लेटर दिया, दिल्ली में ‘कॉलगर्ल’ वाला काम: पीड़ित बोली-कमरे में बंद किया, वीडियो कॉल पर लड़कों को दिखाया; सरकार ने जांच बैठाई
- दिल्ली में अवैध निर्माण वाली इमारतों पर बुलडोजर चलेगा: CM का निर्देश- सभी हॉस्टलों की जांच करें; PG ढहने के मामले में अब तक 5 अरेस्ट
- कर्नाटक मंत्री सतीश जारकीहोली के ठिकानों पर ED रेड: सांसद बेटी के घर समेत 18 जगहों पर तलाशी; मनी लॉन्ड्रिंग केस, पैसे विदेश भेजने का आरोप

items.title: असम में अफसर ने CM-मंत्रियों की आवाज से करोड़ों ठगे:जिला विकास अधिकारी के पद पर है; सरकार ठेका और नौकरी दिलाने के नाम पर वसूली करता
items.summary: असम में राज्य सिविल सर्विस के एक अफसर पर करोड़ों रुपए की ठगी के आरोप लगे हैं। आरोपी देवेश्वर बोरा धेमाजी जिला विकास अधिकारी (DDO) के पद पर हैं। शिकायत के मुताबिक, उन्होंने सरकारी ठेका, नौकरी और शराब की दुकान का लाइसेंस दिलाने के नाम पर लोगों से करोड़ों रुपए ठगे। CM विजिलेंस ने बोरा को मंगलवार को गिरफ्तार किया। जांच में सामने आया है कि ठगी का सिलसिला साल 2011 से चल रहा था। जांच के दौरान CM हिमंत बिस्वा सरमा सहित कई बड़े नेताओं और मंत्रियों की आवाज की नकल कर लोगों को फोन करवाने की बात भी सामने आई
items.body_text:
- Hindi News
- National
- Assam Officer Deveshwar Bora Fraud Case | Mimics CM & Ministers
असम में अफसर ने CM-मंत्रियों की आवाज से करोड़ों ठगे:जिला विकास अधिकारी के पद पर है; सरकार ठेका और नौकरी दिलाने के नाम पर वसूली करता
- कॉपी लिंक
असम में राज्य सिविल सर्विस के एक अफसर पर करोड़ों रुपए की ठगी के आरोप लगे हैं। आरोपी देवेश्वर बोरा धेमाजी जिला विकास अधिकारी (DDO) के पद पर हैं। शिकायत के मुताबिक, उन्होंने सरकारी ठेका, नौकरी और शराब की दुकान का लाइसेंस दिलाने के नाम पर लोगों से करोड़ों रुपए ठगे।
CM विजिलेंस ने बोरा को मंगलवार को गिरफ्तार किया। जांच में सामने आया है कि ठगी का सिलसिला साल 2011 से चल रहा था। जांच के दौरान CM हिमंत बिस्वा सरमा सहित कई बड़े नेताओं और मंत्रियों की आवाज की नकल कर लोगों को फोन करवाने की बात भी सामने आई है।
विजिलेंस के अनुसार, बोरा ने एक व्यक्ति से ₹2 करोड़ और दूसरे से ₹50 लाख लिए। उन पर राजनीतिक नेता रमेन बरठाकुर से भी ₹50 लाख रिश्वत मांगने का आरोप है। इसके अलावा सरकारी बंगले की मरम्मत कराने के बाद ठेकेदार को भुगतान नहीं करने की शिकायत भी सामने आई है। मामले में पीड़ितों की संख्या बढ़ने का अनुमान है।
बड़े नेताओं की आवाज में फोन कर जीतता था भरोसा
CM विजिलेंस की SSP रोजी कलिता के मुताबिक, बोरा लोगों को अपनी ऊंची पहुंच का भरोसा दिलाता था। पीड़ितों ने जांच के दौरान बताया कि बोरा उन्हें बड़े नेताओं और मंत्रियों से फोन पर बात करवाता था।
आरोप है कि मुख्यमंत्री हिमंत बिस्वा सरमा, पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री तरुण गोगोई, मुख्य सचिव और दूसरे बड़े नेताओं-मंत्रियों की आवाज की नकल कर फोन किए जाते थे। इससे लोगों को लगता था कि बोरा की सत्ता के बड़े लोगों तक सीधी पहुंच है और वह उनका काम करवा सकता है।
इसी भरोसे में लोग उसे लाखों-करोड़ों रुपए दे देते थे। कलिता के मुताबिक, बोरा एक व्यक्ति से पैसे लेकर दूसरे व्यक्ति को देता था और इसी रकम से अपना नेटवर्क चलाता था।
बोरा के साथ पूरी टीम काम कर रही थी
जांच में सामने आया है कि बोरा अकेले यह काम नहीं कर रहा था। उसके साथ एक पूरी टीम जुड़ी थी। टीम के सदस्य लोगों से संपर्क करने और ठगी को अंजाम देने में मदद करते थे। विजिलेंस अब इस नेटवर्क से जुड़े लोगों की पहचान और उनकी भूमिका की जांच कर रही है।
CM विजिलेंस ने बताया कि कई पीड़ित उनके पास शिकायत लेकर पहुंचे थे। अलग-अलग शिकायतों और FIR को जोड़कर देवेश्वर बोरा के खिलाफ केस नंबर 14/26 दर्ज किया गया है। जांच में पुराने धोखाधड़ी के मामले सामने आए हैं। एजेंसी अब ठगी की कुल रकम और पीड़ितों की संख्या का पता लगा रही है।
9 मोबाइल मिले, सिर्फ एक सिम बोरा के नाम
जांच के दौरान बोरा के पास से 9 मोबाइल फोन बरामद किए गए। इनमें सिर्फ एक सिम कार्ड उनके नाम पर था, जबकि बाकी सिम दूसरे लोगों के नाम पर पाए गए।
विजिलेंस इन नंबरों के इस्तेमाल की भी जांच कर रही है। यह पता लगाया जा रहा है कि दूसरे लोगों के नाम पर जारी सिम कौन इस्तेमाल करता था। मामले में सूचना प्रौद्योगिकी कानून के तहत संभावित अपराध की भी पड़ताल हो रही है।
परिवार के नाम पर संपत्तियों की भी जांच
विजिलेंस बोरा की आय से अधिक संपत्ति की भी जांच कर रही है। शुरुआती जांच में गुवाहाटी और लखीमपुर में उनकी कथित संपत्तियों की जानकारी सामने आई है। इनमें कुछ संपत्तियां पत्नी और परिवार के दूसरे सदस्यों के नाम पर होने की बात कही गई है।
आरोप है कि बोरा ने कुछ संपत्तियां अपने भाई के नाम पर भी रखीं। जांच अधिकारियों ने उनके भाई का बयान दर्ज किया है। अब बोरा की आय और संपत्तियों का मिलान किया जाएगा।
अरुणाचल में भी धोखाधड़ी का मामला
देवेश्वर बोरा के खिलाफ अरुणाचल प्रदेश में भी धोखाधड़ी का मामला दर्ज होने की जानकारी सामने आई है। असम CM विजिलेंस इसकी भी जांच कर रही है।
फिलहाल जांच एजेंसी बोरा के ठगी नेटवर्क, पैसों के लेन-देन, मोबाइल-सिम और संपत्तियों से जुड़े रिकॉर्ड खंगाल रही है। जांच आगे बढ़ने के साथ इस मामले में और पीड़ितों और आरोपियों के सामने आने की संभावना है।

items.summary: Terror probe on in US mercenary VanDyke case NIA sources amid chargesheet row

Terror probe on in US mercenary VanDyke case: NIA sources amid chargesheet row
The clarification by the NIA comes after a controversy erupted over the agency not invoking the anti-terror law against VanDyke and six Ukrainian nationals who were arrested in a secret operation earlier this year.
The NIA said its investigation into the terror angle against American mercenary Matthew Aaron VanDyke and six Ukrainian nationals was still underway, amid a controversy over the agency not invoking UAPA provisions in its chargesheet. VanDyke, a known name in conflict zones around the world (read a detailed profile, which also examines speculation about VanDyke's CIA links, on him here), and others were arrested in March for allegedly training anti-India ethnic armed groups in Myanmar.
However, controversy erupted on Tuesday after the NIA did not invoke the anti-terror law and charged them under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, which governs the entry and movement of foreigners in India. Interestingly, the NIA had initially charged VanDyke and others under Section 18 of UAPA, which relates to conspiracy to commit terrorist acts.
Curiously, the charges under UAPA were missing in the NIA's chargesheet filed before a special Delhi court on Tuesday. It invited a whirlwind of criticism, with the Congress alleging "pressure" from the US behind the government going soft on VanDyke.
NIA CLARIFIES AMID CHARGESHEET ROW
However, NIA sources clarified that the probe into the terror allegations was not closed. In fact, it was mentioned in the chargesheet itself that the investigation into the terror angle was still on.
The NIA underlined that supplementary chargesheets could be filed as the probe progresses.
The 180-day period of custody for VanDyke and other accused was due to expire on September 8. A chargesheet had to be filed.
The NIA said the chargesheet included the Foreigners Act as the offences under it were established during the course of its investigation. It stressed that the wider investigation into the alleged terror conspiracy remained open.
"Further investigation and supplementary chargesheets remain legally possible," NIA sources said.
The arrest of VanDyke, believed to be part of America's deep state, has particularly drawn attention. Several US officials have raised the issue of his prolonged detention. Last month, his family also appealed to the Donald Trump administration for intervention.
NIA sources said US officials raising the issue was part of normal consular practice and would not determine the outcome of its investigation.
The clarification comes amid intense criticism from the opposition, which castigated the NIA for "dropping" terror charges against the US mercenary.
"If an individual was arrested on allegations involving illegal entry, links with armed groups and drone warfare training, how did those serious allegations suddenly disappear?" Congress MP Abhishek Manu Singhvi tweeted.
Congress spokesperson and Rajya Sabha MP Jairam Ramesh questioned if the decision was taken under "pressure" from the US. "What is the quid pro quo that India expects? This appears to be bullying," Ramesh said.
WHO IS VANDYKE? WHY WAS HE ARRESTED?
VanDyke, who has been part of armed conflicts in Libya and Syria, was detained at Kolkata airport on March 13. The six Ukrainians were picked up at airports in Delhi and Lucknow.
A secretive figure known to live in the shadows, VanDyke has been arrested in the past as well. In 2011, he was taken as a PoW by the then Muammar Gaddafi regime in Libya. He came out only when Gaddafi's regime fell.
He then went on to establish an outfit called Sons of Liberty International (SOLI) - a non-profit security firm that provides military training to armed groups in conflict zones.

Rahul Gandhi double your age: Shehzad Poonawalla counters Riya Ahir's uncle jibe
A war of words erupted between Mumbai-based model Riya Ahir and former BJP spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla after he mocked her for failing to secure a Bigg Boss 20 entry. Ahir called Poonawalla "uncle", which he countered with a Rahul Gandhi jibe.
Mumbai-based model Riya Ahir, who shot to fame after a video of her stopping a police van during the Gen Z protests went viral, has sparred with former BJP national spokesperson and Congress rebel Shehzad Poonawalla after he mocked her failure to enter Bigg Boss 20. Poonawalla, a prominent political commentator had targeted Ahir in a reel that also criticised journalist Arfa Khanum Sherwani.
Ahir was competing against Punjabi actress Love Gill for a public-voted spot on Bigg Boss Season 20. Gill won the vote, leaving Ahir out of the show before she could enter the house.
In his reel, Shehzad Poonawalla alleged that Ahir's viral protest photograph was part of a political strategy. "The plan was completely set," he claimed, alleging that the photo would first be made viral as part of a protest, followed by political platforms "from Rahul Gandhi to Raj Thackeray", before the alleged "propaganda" was taken into the Bigg Boss house to push an "anti-Modi agenda".
"There is a big difference between making a scripted photo go viral, getting platforms from Rahul Gandhi to Supriya Sule, Raj Thackeray and Dimple Yadav [to follow the account], [and] entering the Bigg Boss house, and winning a popular mandate from the public," Poonawalla said.
He claimed Ahir had the backing of what he described as a "Left-wing ecosystem" and "anti-Modi YouTubers", and mocked the political support he said she had received.
"Rahul Gandhi, who lost 99 elections and cannot even win one election for the Congress, was supposed to secure what kind of online support for you?" Poonawalla said.
Shehzad Poonawalla also called Ahir's defeat an "epic humiliation" for the "entire Left ecosystem", which he claimed had presented her as "the face of Gen Z". He contrasted her with Gill, describing Gill as someone who "visits temples, goes to gurdwaras, serves cows, respects the Indian Army and does not use abusive language".
He also highlighted a remark Ahir made during the Bigg Boss selection process. During an exchange with Gill, Ahir corrected her for referring to the vehicle she had stopped during the protest as a bus.
When Gill said she was thinking that if the driver had not stopped, "maybe she would not be here today", Ahir replied, "The purpose of my life would have been fulfilled then".
Gill then said she believed Ahir's work was "outside" the Bigg Boss house, not inside, where people could fight for their rights.
Poonawalla seized on Ahir's remark in his reel, arguing that it demonstrated why she had been rejected by viewers. "Riya Ahir was not even evicted," he said, adding, "Her entry itself did not happen."
LEAVE GIRLS HALF YOUR AGE ALONE
Ahir responded with two reels, the first beginning with a deliberately mocking reference to Poonawalla.
"Namaste, respected Shehzaab, Shehbaz, Shehzaab, Poonawala Uncle," she said. "I just saw the reel you made about me. Well, I'm flattered," she said.
"But at the same time, I just want to request you to keep your big nose out of my personal business and life," she added.
Ahir, 28, then accused Poonawalla, aged 38, of having an old business of "cornering young girls".
"You are more than twice my age, so I would just request you to go do politics with people of your own age and men like you, not little girls," she said.
She denied being affiliated with the political figures named by Poonawalla and said the allegations against her appeared to follow a common script used by other influencers.

items.title: Pakistan walking the tightrope as US-Iran tensions soar, admits Khawaja Asif
items.summary: Pakistan walking the tightrope as USIran tensions soar admits Khawaja Asif
items.body_text:
Pakistan walking the tightrope as US-Iran tensions soar, admits Khawaja Asif
Khawaja Asif said Pakistan would seek to preserve its diplomatic room for manoeuvre by maintaining communication with both Washington and Tehran, exercising restraint and avoiding steps that could further complicate its ties with either side.
Pakistan Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has admitted that Islamabad is facing a delicate diplomatic challenge amid escalating tensions between the United States and Iran, describing Pakistan’s position as a "tightrope walk" given its close relations with both Iran and the Gulf countries involved in the conflict.
Pakistan has sought to play a mediating role between the US and Iran in efforts to end the war in West Asia, but discussions so far have failed to produce a permanent settlement.
Asif said Pakistan has "brotherly relations" with all sides and would have to carefully assess how far it could go in any further mediation efforts between Washington and Tehran. Islamabad would also have to consider whether it could avoid taking certain steps that might further complicate its diplomatic position.
"For Pakistan, this becomes quite a test, how far we can go in this conflict, where we can exercise restraint, and whether we can even afford to stay away," the minister said in an interview with Geo News, adding, "All these considerations, in my view, make it a tightrope walk for Pakistan".
He was speaking about Pakistan’s possible further role in efforts to engage both sides as tensions continue to simmer across the region.
Asif said Islamabad had been trying to maintain communication with both the US and Iran, stressing that its relationships with all countries involved were important.
"The way we have tried to contact both sides, we have tried to call them," he said.
He underlined that Pakistan's ties with the Gulf states involved in the conflict were as important to Islamabad as its relationship with Iran.
"We have brotherly relations with all the Gulf countries involved in this conflict, as well as with Iran on the other side. These relations are very dear to us," Asif said.
The minister indicated that Islamabad would seek to preserve as much diplomatic space as possible and avoid, where feasible, actions that could further narrow its room for manoeuvre.
"For Pakistan, this becomes a kind of special situation. We have to see how far we can go and whether we can avoid (taking certain steps) if possible," he said.
Asif also said Pakistan should continue to hope for a diplomatic way out of the crisis.
"And we should keep hoping that some way forward will emerge," he added.
Asked about the possibility of further action or Pakistan's response to developments involving its partners, Asif said Islamabad did not necessarily have to respond to every action in an identical manner.

items.title: 'Give us keys or we go on hunger strike': Kashmiri Pandit hold silent protest in Srinagar, demand secure housing amid LeT terror threats
items.summary: Kashmiri Pandit employees protest in Srinagar over delayed secure housing and warn of an indefinite hunger strike after September 30 amid fresh terror threats.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: Zee News. Kashmiri Pandit employees hold silent protest in Srinagar.
- News
- Photos
- Videos
Kashmiri Pandit employees under the Prime Minister’s Package held a silent protest in Srinagar on Wednesday, demanding secure government accommodation amid fresh terror threats. Employees living in rented houses said the lack of security has increased their fear and stress. They gave the administration until September 30 to allot completed transit units or face an indefinite hunger strike, escalating pressure on authorities.
Representatives of the employees gathered at Press Colony and said about 3,500 of their colleagues are still living in rented accommodation across the Valley. They said many private houses do not have proper security.
The employees also alleged that several transit buildings are complete, but possession has not been handed over to them. They said repeated government assurances and deadlines have failed to resolve the issue.
Ashish Razdan, a Kashmiri Pandit employee, said the demand for safe accommodation has continued for years. He said employees have been waiting since 2010 and questioned why completed buildings have not been opened.
He said, “Our major demand is something we have been raising with the government for years. We have been here since 2010, it has been 16 years and we still have not been provided safe accommodation. We have been given deadline after deadline: first April, then May, June, July, August, and now the administration has given us September-end as the deadline. I don’t understand why, when some of the buildings are already complete, we cannot be given possession of them. Out of the 39 buildings, 26 are ready for occupation. Why can’t we be shifted to these buildings immediately? Construction on the remaining buildings can continue alongside."
"September 30 is our deadline. If our demand is not addressed by then, we will be forced to go on hunger strike. Every time a threat letter is issued against us, the stress is immense. Today, we have gathered to come out and speak to the media,” he added.
The employees said several buildings have received the required clearances, but the handover process remains stalled. They said the government is providing security, but their immediate concern is safe accommodation following a series of threat letters.
Barkha, a Kashmiri Pandit employee, said the employees have waited for years for accommodation in transit camps. She said the recent threats have added to their concerns and called for completed buildings to be opened immediately.
“We have gathered here because we have been waiting for accommodation in the transit camps for years. The government has been assuring us that we will be accommodated, but nothing has happened so far. Now, with these fresh threat letters coming in, our concerns have increased. Our demand is very simple: the buildings that are already ready should be opened and we should be shifted there immediately. it will also be easier for the government to provide us with proper security. This has become a huge mental stress for us," she said.
The employees said they will begin an indefinite protest and hunger strike if secure housing is not provided by September 30.
The protest comes amid fresh terror threats targeting Kashmiri Pandit employees appointed under the PM Package. Letters attributed to the Lashkar-e-Taiba-linked United Liberation Council have reportedly warned employees to leave their jobs or face death.
Personal details, including phone numbers, home addresses and vehicle registration numbers, were also allegedly leaked online and circulated through social media and messaging platforms.

items.title: KTR, Harish Rao among 22 BRS lawmakers suspended for remainder of Telangana monsoon session
items.summary: Twenty-two BRS legislators, including KTR and Harish Rao, were suspended for the remainder of the Telangana Assembly's monsoon session after entering the well to protest.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: REPRESENTATIVE PICTURE
Twenty-two legislators of Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) have been debarred from attending the Telangana Assembly for the rest of the term of the monsoon session for the disruption of the proceedings by rushing to the well and raising slogans. The punitive action was taken on Wednesday following the refusal by the opposition legislators to heed the repeated calls of Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar and the government representatives to vacate the well.
The matter came to the boiling point owing to the demand to discuss the police highhandedness issue related to the BRS women MLAs and the attacks made against the party president K Chandrasekhar Rao.
The working president of BRS K T Rama Rao moved for an adjournment motion regarding the police highhandedness issue raised days back and also the remarks against the party leadership.
Defying Speaker requests: Defying the Chair despite repeated requests made by the Speaker, the Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, and the Legislative Affairs Minister D Sridhar Babu, BRS legislators charged into the well of the House making slogans.
Speaker's assurances: Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar assured that he would go through all the formal written submissions made on the issues raised by the opposition, but the lawmakers failed to relent.
The Cabinet members harshly criticized the actions of the opposition, mentioning the previous instances of protest and allegations of caste discrimination.
Well-wishes from ruling party: Deputy CM Bhatti Vikramarka on record expressed well-wishes of the ruling Congress leaders for KCR, wishing him a long and healthy political life.
Regarding purification ceremonies: Vikramarka referred to media reports regarding the conduct of purification ceremonies by BRS leaders near the farmhouse of KCR after the protests made by Dalits against the allegations made by the BRS MLC Tata Madhusudhan against the Speaker.
Defending self-respect: Claiming that the ruling side would not take any more insults, the discussion revolved around self-respect of the institution as well as the chair.
Since there are 37 members in total BRS strength in the 119-member assembly, the mass suspension will leave more than half of the party strength suspended during the rest of the session period.
Key leaders penalised: The suspension order targets high-profile figures, including K T Rama Rao, T Harish Rao, G Jagadish Reddy, P Sabita Indra Reddy, and Vemula Prashant Reddy.
Formal motion: Legislative Affairs Minister D Sridhar Babu moved the formal suspension motion, which was immediately enacted by the chair following unyielding disruptions.
Remaining roster: The sweeping measure benches over half of the opposition bench, drastically altering the floor dynamic for upcoming legislative business.

items.title: Who is Rohan Parekh? 24-year-old man arrested for posing as fake PMO ID Card
items.summary: Two men accused of posing as PMO officials were remanded in police custody until September 11 after allegedly attempting to enter Mumbai’s Jio World Plaza with a suspicious PMO identity card and a licensed firearm ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s scheduled visit.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: Screengrab/X/ANI
A court has remanded the two arrested individuals, who allegedly posed as PMO officials, to police custody until September 11. Mumbai Police arrested them while they were allegedly attempting to enter the venue where Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to attend an event.
According to police, three men allegedly used a suspicious government-issued identity card and forced their way past mall security while carrying a firearm to gain entry to Jio World Plaza in Mumbai’s BKC area.
"Three men allegedly used a suspicious government ID card and forced their way, armed with a firearm, past mall security into Jio World Plaza, BKC. An FIR has been filed at BKC PS under various BNS sections, including impersonation of a public servant and unlawful entry armed with a weapon. Crime Branch is conducting further investigation. The weapon has been found to be licensed, and two persons have been arrested in this regard. Please note that this incident took place yesterday", Mumbai police said.
Who is Rohan Parekh?
At 24, Rohan Premal Parekh has studied in London, holds a BSc in Mathematics and Science, and has developed an interest in drone technology, according to the Indian Express. However, on Monday, the young businessman was taken into police custody after allegedly using a suspected Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) identity card to gain entry to Jio World Plaza in Mumbai’s BKC, a day before Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s scheduled visit to the area.
Parikh, who works as a share broker, had reached the premises with his friend Prathamesh Ganesh Bagul, 26, and his personal security guard, Dilip Rajaram Kunde, 49, a retired Army personnel from rural Nashik. Kunde, who retired from the Army around a decade ago, had been working as Parikh’s bodyguard.
According to police, Kunde was carrying a licensed revolver and six live cartridges when the trio entered the premises.
Investigators are now examining Parikh’s background in drone technology as part of their efforts to determine why he was carrying an identity card that identified him as a PMO official.
The identity card allegedly described Parikh as a Grade C official of the PMO and stated that he was associated with drone technology.
According to police, Parikh, Bagul and Kunde arrived at Jio World Plaza at around 4.50 pm on Monday. During the security screening, one of them allegedly presented the identity card and claimed to be associated with the PMO. Security personnel subsequently alerted the police. Investigators then traced Parikh using CCTV footage and details of the vehicle in which the three men had arrived.
A police team visited Parikh’s residence in Khar later that night. He was at home and, according to the police remand application, told investigators that Kunde and Bagul had accompanied him. Parikh was subsequently detained, while Kunde was arrested in Kalyan. Bagul, who has been friends with Parikh for the past few years, has also been named as an accused and remains absconding.

items.title: India becomes the only country with a fully electrified dedicated freight corridor: How the Modi Government turned a two-decade-old project into reality
items.summary: The freight corridor will not be limited to the Eastern and Western corridors and is set to be expanded.
items.body_text:
In a major infrastructural achievement, India’s ambitious rail infrastructure development project, the Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC), became fully operational. On Tuesday (September 8, 2026), Prime Minister Modi inaugurated the final sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC), one of the two parts of the DFC.
The Prime Minister inaugurated three remaining sections of the WDFC, namely, New Sanand-North-New Makarpura, New Umbergaon-New Saphale, and New Saphale-New JNPT. The sections stretched up to 326 km were built at a cost of over ₹20,700 crore. They link the Jawaharlal Nehru Port in Mumbai, Maharashtra, with Dadri in Uttar Pradesh, where it intersects with the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor (EDFC).
With the inauguration of three sections, the entire stretch of 2,843-km dedicated freight network, combining the 1,506-km WDFC and the 1,337-km-long Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor (EDFC), has become operational.
Modi government made the project a reality
The freight network project was conceived in 2004, during the BJP coalition government led by the late Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. In 2006, the two corridors were approved by the UPA-I government led by the late PM Manmohan Singh. The Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) was incorporated to execute the project.
However, the project existed only on paper till 2014, after which the project was revived by the Modi government. The government resolved the long-pending issues that blocked the project, and it finally became a reality about two decades after its approval.
India is the only country with a fully electrified DFC
With the completion of the DFC, India has become the only country with a fully electrified dedicated freight corridor built for routine double-stack container operations. The electric double-stack arrangement enables two containers to be carried one above the other, leading to reduced time and fuel consumption and more cargo per train.
The rail tracks in the EDFC and the WDFC have been specifically designed for the electric double-stack arrangement, with overhead wires fitted higher than usual. Even though both corridors are capable of double-stack container operations, they are more prominent on the WDFC. The cargo on the EDFC mostly carries coal, steel, food grain, and other bulk mineral freight.
As per the railways, the DFCCIL handled approximately 5.21 lakh freight train trips, averaging around 435 trains per day as of August 31, 2026. The DFCCIL has generated approximately 658 billion Gross Tonne Kilometres (GTKM) and 360 billion Net Tonne Kilometres (NTKM). At present, 27% of the total freight is carried via rail route. The National Rail Plan intends to increase this share by 45% by 2030. In the last financial year, the Railways recorded its highest-ever loading of 1,670 million tonnes.
The Eastern and the Western freight corridors
The existing freight network comprises the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor (EDFC) and the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor. The EDFC starts from New Sahnewal in Punjab and extends up to New Sonnagar in Bihar via Haryana and Uttar Pradesh and connects four states: Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar.
The EDFC from Ludhiana (Punjab) to Sonnagar (Bihar) became fully operational in October 2023. Subsequently, a proposed 538-km Sonnagar-Dankuni (West Bengal) extension was taken out of the sanctioned DFC project and planned separately under the PPP model.
The WDFC starts from New Dadri in Uttar Pradesh and extends up to New Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT) in Maharashtra. It links the National Capital Region and the industrial belts of northern and western India directly to the country’s busiest container port while passing through Haryana, Rajasthan, and Gujarat.

items.title: ECI clarifies C.N.R. Rao SIR row: No notice issued to Bharat Ratna scientist or his family over name discrepancy
items.summary: The ECI also clarified that it has not served any notice to Rao or his family so far, taking into account his stature and contribution to the country.
items.body_text:
The Election Commission of India (ECI) has denied reports that Bharat Ratna awardee and eminent scientist Professor C.N.R. Rao was served a notice over a “self-name mismatch” during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Karnataka.
The clarification came after reports claimed that Rao had been asked to appear for a hearing because of a discrepancy in his name between the 2002 electoral roll and the current voter list. According to those reports, his name appeared as “Prof. C.N.R. Rao” in the older roll, while the current roll reportedly mentioned it as “Proff. C.N.R. Rao”, with an additional “f”.
However, the ECI clarified that this information is “factually incorrect”.
According to the Commission, Rao’s name in the 2002 electoral roll actually appears as “Rama S/O H. Nagesh”, while the current electoral roll lists him as “Proff. C.N.R. Rao S/O Nagesh Rav. H.” The ECI also clarified that it has not served any notice to Rao or his family so far, taking into account his stature and contribution to the country.
ECI rejects ‘extra f’ claim
The clarification effectively rules out the earlier claim that Rao was asked to appear before election officials because the word “Prof” had been incorrectly recorded as “Proff”.
Reports had said that the 92-year-old scientist was facing a “self-name mismatch” and that a hearing had been scheduled in Bengaluru’s Malleshwaram area, near the Indian Institute of Science (IISc).
The latest ECI statement, however, makes it clear that no such notice has been issued to Rao or his family at present. It also specifically rejected the claim that the alleged notice was linked to an extra “f” in his name.
C.N.R. Rao’s contribution to science
Prof. C.N.R. Rao has made major contributions to solid-state and structural chemistry and is considered one of the most decorated scientists in his field. His work has covered areas including solid-state materials, nanomaterials and structural chemistry, helping open new areas of research in modern chemistry.
He founded the Solid State and Structural Chemistry Unit at IISc in 1976 and later served as the institute’s director from 1984 to 1994. He also founded the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR) in Jakkur and served as its founding president.
His contribution was not limited to scientific research. Rao also played an important role in shaping India’s science and research policies. Over the years, he has received several major national and international honours.
Bharat Ratna among several major honours
Rao has received some of the country’s highest civilian honours and several major international awards. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India’s highest civilian honour, and became the third scientist to receive the award.
His other honours include the Padma Vibhushan, Padma Shri and Karnataka Ratna, besides numerous other awards and recognitions.
Earlier reports had raised questions
The reports about the alleged SIR notice had attracted attention because of Rao’s age and stature as a Bharat Ratna awardee. A representative from his office had earlier said that they had not received any physical notice.
“It appears to have been put online on the ECI website. I am not clear about that one; I have not seen it,” the representative had said. The representative had also said that, apart from the alleged additional letter in “Proff”, there did not appear to be any other issue with the electoral records.
“According to the office records and email, there is no notice as of now. A physical letter also has not reached us,” the representative said.
However, following the ECI’s latest clarification, those earlier reports cannot be treated as an accurate account of the current position. The Commission has specifically denied issuing such a notice to Rao or his family and has rejected the claim about the alleged “extra f” mismatch.

items.title: US accuses Chinese AI companies of doing industrial-scale distillation of American AI models: Read what it means
items.summary: The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Agency, along with other key authorities have accused Chinese AI companies of conducting industrial-scale distillation of AI models of OpenAI, Claude, Grok, and others to extract proprietary capabilities, thus reducing development timelines and costs for their own AI models.
items.body_text:
Days after claiming to have disrupted a Chinese botnet network that was allegedly targeting American critical infrastructure, the US has accused Chinese AI companies of ‘copying’ proprietary functionalities and capabilities of US AI companies. America’s Cyber Defense Agency, Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), said in a release issued on 8th September that Chinese AI companies are conducting “industrial-scale knowledge distillation campaigns” to extract proprietary capabilities from leading AI models.
“China-based artificial intelligence (AI) companies are conducting systematic extraction of proprietary functionalities and capabilities of U.S. AI companies’ models through industrial-scale knowledge distillation campaigns that form the core—not merely a supplement—of their AI development strategy,” the press release stated.
The US authorities acknowledged that distillation is a legitimate and useful technique in AI research. However, the US officials claimed that China-based AI companies are engaging in “aggressive, malicious, and targeted distillation activities at an industrial scale that extract restricted proprietary functionalities and capabilities of U.S. frontier AI models.”
DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Alibaba and other Chinese AI companies with CCP awareness are extracting capabilities of top US AI models like Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Grok
US officials have alleged that top Chinese AI models DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, MiniMax, StepFun, and Z.AI extracted “billions of tokens across millions of exchanges/requests” from US frontier AI models, including variants of Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Grok, since at least late 2024. These alleged distillation campaigns are allegedly being conducted with Chinese government awareness.
The US authorities alleged that since 2024, DeepSeek has conducted organised distillation campaigns targeting reasoning capabilities, specialised optimisations, and domain-specific functions to train its R1 and V3 models.
Similarly, Alibaba allegedly leveraged industrial-scale distillation to improve its Qwen family of AI models.
The US authorities claimed that top Chinese AI models, including Moonshot AI, MiniMax, Stepfun, and Z.AI, also engaged in “malicious knowledge distillation of U.S. AI companies’ models.”
“Likely with Chinese government awareness, DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, MiniMax, StepFun, and Z.AI extracted billions of tokens across millions of exchanges/requests from U.S. frontier AI models, including variants of Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Grok, since at least late 2024. DeepSeek has conducted organized campaigns since at least 2024 targeting reasoning capabilities, specialized optimizations, and domain-specific functions to train its R1 and V3 models. Alibaba leveraged industrial-scale distillation to improve the company’s Qwen family of AI models. Moonshot AI, MiniMax, Stepfun, and Z.AI also engaged in malicious knowledge distillation of U.S. AI companies’ models,” the US officials said.
The modus operandi
Explaining the modus operandi of the Chinese distillation campaigns targeting US frontier AI models, the US authorities said that several top Chinese AI companies route distillation requests via multiple pathways to obtain unauthorised access and violate the terms of the targeted US AI companies.
These pathways include native application programming interfaces (APIs), remote cloud providers, and third-party aggregators that automatically obfuscate user metadata to avoid detection.
In addition, the China-based AI companies allegedly use a gray market of proxies known as “transfer stations” to bypass geographic restrictions placed by US AI companies.

items.title: Trump Says US and Canada Have Reached Last-Minute Deal to Delay 50% US Tariffs on Canadian Imports
items.summary: The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
items.body_text:
Trump Says US and Canada Have Reached Last-Minute Deal to Delay 50% US Tariffs on Canadian Imports
The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
- World News
- 4 min read
Washington: President Donald Trump said Tuesday he was delaying 50% U.S. tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian imports after the two countries reached a last-minute deal hours before the sanctions were to go into effect.
The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
“I have paused the 50% Tariffs against Canada, that were scheduled to kick in tomorrow morning for three days, based on the fact that Canada and the U.S.A., subject to the finalisation of documents, have a DEAL!” Trump posted on Truth Social less than two hours before the 12:01 a.m. Wednesday deadline.
If they had gone into effect as scheduled at 12:01 a.m. Wednesday, Trump’s import taxes would have hit Canadian products ranging from hockey sticks to tongue depressors.
Advertisement
But the political impact would likely have been bigger than the economic one. Canada had threatened to retaliate against any new tariffs with levies of its own, aggravating a trade fight between countries that sold each other $880 billion worth of goods and services last year.
Canadian officials did not immediately respond to requests for comment Tuesday night.
Advertisement
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Trump had spoken twice by phone in the past two days about the ongoing negotiations, including a call Tuesday afternoon, Carney’s office said, underscoring the last-minute push for a deal.
Both countries had reason to step back from the brink. Nearly 72% of Canada’s goods exports last year went to the United States. And the Trump administration would be taking a risk by imposing a hefty new tariff — paid by U.S. importers who try to pass along the cost to consumers via higher prices — ahead of November’s midterm elections. U.S. voters are already frustrated with the high cost of living.
“I don’t think either side really wants these tariffs to come into effect,’’ Ryan Majerus, a partner at King & Spalding and a former U.S. trade official, said before the delay was announced. “There’s a pretty strong push on both sides to find an off-ramp here.’’
Trump’s approach to dealing with Canada marks an extraordinary departure from the traditionally cooperative relationship between the two countries. Trump has hit Canadian goods with tariffs — in a push to bring manufacturing back to the U.S. — and has repeatedly made inflammatory comments about turning Canada into America’s 51st state.
Trump has made tariffs the centrepiece of his second-term economic agenda. Last year, he imposed double-digit import taxes on almost every country, justifying them by declaring the longstanding U.S. trade deficit a national emergency. The Supreme Court in February ruled that he’d overstepped his authority, striking down those tariffs and setting the stage for the federal government to pay refunds to importers.
So Trump has looked for other legal authority to impose tariffs.
To hit Canada, he reached back to the Great Depression, invoking Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 to threaten 50% tariffs on products that account for about 5% of Canadian exports to the United States.
Nearly a century ago, with the U.S. and world economies in collapse, Congress passed the 1930 tariff law, imposing taxes on imports from around the world. Known as the Smoot-Hawley tariffs, named for their congressional sponsors, they are notorious among economists and historians for limiting world commerce and making the Great Depression worse.
Section 338 tariffs have never been used before.
Section 338 authorises the president to impose tariffs of up to 50% on imports from count
