TOLEDO
El nuevo aparcamiento disuasorio del Polígono encara sus obras tras formalizarse el acta de replanteo
La Junta de Gobierno del Ayuntamiento avanza en varios proyectos ya anunciados y prepara además autobuses gratuitos por el Día Mundial sin Coche el próximo 22 de septiembre
TOLEDO
Comienzan las obras del nuevo aparcamiento del Polígono. La Junta de Gobierno Local del Ayuntamiento de Toledo ha tomado conocimiento este miércoles de la formalización del acta de replanteo de los trabajos de adecuación de un espacio público para uso de este aparcamiento disuasorio de ... más de 500 plazas en el barrio del Polígono, junto al Hospital Universitario de Toledo, una actuación comprometida por el alcalde, Carlos Velázquez, que cuenta con un presupuesto de 169.931,27 euros y un plazo de ejecución de tres meses.
El portavoz municipal, Juan José Alcalde, ha señalado que este nuevo aparcamiento tiene como objetivo «aliviar el tráfico, regular mejor los aparcamientos y que la gente tenga espacio suficiente para poder aparcar». Con la formalización del acta de replanteo se da un nuevo paso para la ejecución de una actuación que busca mejorar la disponibilidad de estacionamiento en esta zona de la ciudad. Se trata de una intervención especialmente esperada en una zona que desde la apertura del nuevo hospital soporta una elevada presión circulatoria. Aunque el complejo sanitario dispone de aparcamientos propios, el incremento constante de usuarios ha provocado que numerosos conductores recurran desde hace años a estacionar en solares sin acondicionar situados en las inmediaciones.
Noticia relacionada
Por otro lado, la Junta de Gobierno Local también ha iniciado el expediente de modificación no prevista de las inversiones asociadas al contrato de prestación de servicios de depuración de aguas residuales de Toledo. Según ha explicado el portavoz municipal, la modificación responde a la detección de «determinados elementos cuyo estado era peor del previsto inicialmente» y que requieren incrementar la inversión prevista para garantizar «su adecuada solución». El objetivo de este expediente es, por tanto, adaptar las inversiones asociadas al contrato a las necesidades detectadas durante su desarrollo, después de comprobar el estado de algunos elementos que requieren una actuación superior a la inicialmente contemplada.
Obras en el centro de mayores
Otro de los asuntos abordados ha sido la ampliación, por un mes y siete días, del plazo de ejecución de las obras del Centro de Mayores de Buenavista. El nuevo plazo establece que los trabajos deberán estar finalizados el próximo 30 de septiembre.
Alcalde ha destacado que se trata de una infraestructura «largamente reivindicada por los vecinos» y ha asegurado que «va a ser una realidad dentro de poco». El portavoz ha recordado además que la semana pasada la Junta de Gobierno Local aprobó la adjudicación del mobiliario del centro, tanto el correspondiente a la cocina como al resto del equipamiento necesario para que pueda comenzar a funcionar una vez concluyan las obras.
El Gobierno municipal ha defendido que durante la actual legislatura el proyecto fue consensuado con los vecinos del barrio, lo que permitió ampliar el centro y adaptar sus instalaciones a las necesidades planteadas. Además, el edificio queda preparado para una futura segunda fase que permitiría incorporar una nueva planta.
Autobuses sin coste el 22 de septiembre
En materia de movilidad, la Junta de Gobierno Local ha dado el visto bueno a la gratuidad de los autobuses urbanos de Toledo el próximo 22 de septiembre, con motivo de la celebración del Día Mundial sin Coche.
La medida se suma a la gratuidad del transporte público prevista para este fin de semana con motivo de las Noches del Patrimonio. En este caso, los autobuses urbanos serán gratuitos entre las 19:00 y las 00:00 horas.

Según ha informado la consejera Portavoz del Gobierno regional, Esther Padilla, este miércoles en la rueda de prensa posterior al Consejo de Gobierno, la actuación contempla una ayuda de 200.000 euros para las obras d
items.body_text:
CASTILLA-LA MANCHA
La Junta destina 1,4 millones a recuperar el castillo de Escalona y los molinos de Consuegra
El Gobierno regional aportará 200.000 euros para el castillo y 1,2 millones para restaurar e iluminar el conjunto de Consuegra
Toledo
El Gobierno de Castilla-La Mancha ha aprobado ayudas por un importe conjunto de 1,4 millones de euros para actuaciones de conservación y mejora de dos de los principales conjuntos patrimoniales de la provincia de Toledo: el castillo de Escalona y los molinos ... de viento de Consuegra.
Según ha informado la consejera Portavoz del Gobierno regional, Esther Padilla, este miércoles en la rueda de prensa posterior al Consejo de Gobierno, la actuación contempla una ayuda de 200.000 euros para las obras de reconstrucción del castillo de Escalona, después del derrumbe que sufrió parte de la fortaleza el pasado mes de marzo y que provocó daños materiales.
200.000
euros
Reconstrucción del castillo de Escalona después del derrumbe de una torre el pasado mes de marzo
Tras el incidente, técnicos de Patrimonio se desplazaron hasta el municipio toledano para evaluar los elementos afectados y comprobar también el estado del resto del edificio. La ayuda permitirá intervenir en la zona dañada y avanzar en la conservación de una fortaleza que fue adquirida por el Ayuntamiento de Escalona en 2024.
Noticia relacionada
En el caso de Consuegra, el Ejecutivo autonómico ha aprobado una ayuda de 194.000 euros para la restauración de los molinos de viento situados en el cerro Calderico. Los trabajos permitirán reparar los daños ocasionados a finales de enero por un temporal de viento que alcanzó rachas de hasta 90 kilómetros por hora. Seis molinos resultaron afectados: dos sufrieron importantes daños en sus aspas, mientras que otros cuatro registraron desperfectos en las cubiertas y los ejes.
194.000
euros
Restauración de los molinos de viento afectados por un temporal el pasado mes de enero
Los daños obligaron a restringir temporalmente el acceso al cerro Calderico y tuvieron también consecuencias sobre el desarrollo habitual de las actividades turísticas del municipio.
La portavoz del Gobierno regional ha recordado que los molinos de Consuegra están declarados Bien de Interés Cultural (BIC) y constituyen «una de las imágenes más reconocibles de Castilla-La Mancha dentro y fuera de nuestra región».
Un millón para la iluminación
A la restauración se suma una inversión de un millón de euros para renovar la iluminación ornamental del castillo y los molinos de Consuegra, un compromiso adquirido por el presidente regional, Emiliano García-Page, con el municipio. La actuación se ejecutará entre 2026 y 2027 y supondrá sustituir el actual sistema de iluminación por tecnología LED de alta eficiencia, además de incorporar un sistema de gestión inteligente.
1.000.000
euros
Renovación de la iluminación ornamental del castillo y de los molinos de Consuegra
El proyecto contempla la instalación de 187 proyectores, de los que 92 estarán destinados al castillo y otros 95 a las fachadas de los 12 molinos. También se colocarán 49 balizas a lo largo de todo el recorrido.
Padilla ha destacado la importancia turística del conjunto, señalando que Consuegra recibió el pasado año más de 15.000 visitantes al mes. La nueva iluminación permitirá mejorar todavía más la imagen nocturna de uno de los principales reclamos patrimoniales y turísticos de la provincia de Toledo.

items.title: Welcome to Trumpapalooza, the unusual convention Republicans hope will save the midterm elections
items.summary: Dozens of candidates in tight districts have skipped the MAGA conclave convened to glorify Donald Trump, fearing the toxic influence of the president
items.body_text:
Welcome to Trumpapalooza, the unusual convention Republicans hope will save the midterm elections
Dozens of candidates in tight districts have skipped the MAGA conclave convened to glorify Donald Trump, fearing the toxic influence of the president
Donald Trump announced in June that he would hold “a truly historic event.” The hyperbole is typical for him, but the timing is unusual: a Republican Party convention in Dallas, Texas, less than two months before the midterm elections.
The Trump rendezvous with history takes place on September 9 and 10. And it is true that it is unprecedented. It is being billed like the kind of conclave both parties stage every four years, shortly before presidential elections, to pick their nominees and display coalition unity — but this time it promises to be more of a damage-control operation: polls ahead of November 3 favor the Democrats. All seats in the House and one-third of the Senate are at stake, and it is possible the Republicans could lose control of one or both chambers — and with it, the legislative initiative.
The gathering already has an informal name: Trumpapalooza. It is nicknamed after a famous rock festival, Lollapalooza, but also as a clear signal: like almost everything happening in the Republican Party since his return to power, what takes place over the next two days at the American Airlines Stadium in Dallas will revolve around Trump.
The difference is that the 50,000 people who traveled from across the country to attend the Republican convention in Milwaukee a couple of years ago — held a few days after the then-candidate survived an assassination attempt at an outdoor rally — arrived with more enthusiasm than the 20,000 attendees the organizers say they expect in Dallas. But the menus will look similar: a diet of America First candidate speeches, all the MAGA pageantry and excess, a playlist of the leader’s favorite songs — including one in particular, Lee Greenwood’s God Bless the U.S.A. — and not one but two Trump rallies, which will be “like no other,” he promised in June.
Two nights in a row
Scheduling the main act for two consecutive nights was the organizers’ gambit to prevent interest from flagging among attendees, who were asked to consider a $25,000 donation to participate. Wednesday will be Trump’s major address, which is expected to combine a defense of his administration’s policies — which critics say have raised the cost of living and pushed up gas prices because of tariffs and an unpopular war in Iran with no quick end in sight — with a reaffirmation of MAGA ideals: a sealed southern border and a turn toward isolationism to promote American values. On Thursday, the president will speak after his running mate, J. D. Vance, to close out the event.
That fewer than half of Republican candidates in competitive districts appear on the roster shows how difficult it has become for the president to meet one of the convention’s stated goals (besides stroking his ego and rallying a demoralized party base): helping those who face the toughest November fights in contests that are uncertain. With Democrats betting everything on turning the vote into a referendum on Trump’s presidency, for struggling GOP hopefuls he has become more a liability than an electoral asset.
Thus, in a party that for two years has rarely contradicted its leader, this convention has prompted many politicians to take a stand. Senators such as Tommy Tuberville (Alabama), John Cornyn (Texas) and Mike Rounds (South Dakota), and House members running for reelection such as David Valadao (California), Mike LaLota (New York) and Juan Ciscomani (Arizona) are not expected in Dallas, U.S. media outlets that have been tracking attendance at Trumpapalooza report. Excuses vary, but conservative commentator Jay Nordlinger summed them up wryly with an “old piece of American slang”: “They’ve got a hair appointment that day.”

items.title: United States says it destroyed five Iranian tankers
items.summary: The two opposing forces exchanged fresh attacks on Tuesday after the Revolutionary Guard opened fire on US warships
items.body_text:
United States says it destroyed five Iranian tankers
The two opposing forces exchanged fresh attacks on Tuesday after the Revolutionary Guard opened fire on US warships
The United States and Iran on Tuesday engaged in a new exchange of attacks, another step in the escalation of hostilities in a war that Vice President J. D. Vance refuses to describe as such. Central Command, responsible for U.S. forces in the Middle East, confirmed the destruction of five tankers linked to Iran in the Persian Gulf in response to two attacks carried out by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps against a U.S. warship in the previous two days.
On its account on the social network X, Central Command (CENTCOM) said the tankers struck were part of the network that helps fund the Iranian regime and the groups Tehran’s sponsors in the Middle East together, adding that they were linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). One of them, the Derya, was hit near Kharg Island, the heart of Iran’s oil industry. The other four — the Kaviz, the Charminar, the Horizon 1 and the Riesco — were destroyed in the Gulf of Oman.
“American forces directed the crews to abandon ship before the vessels were struck and rendered inoperable,” the statement said, adding that no U.S. service members were injured in the operation. CENTCOM also recalled that over the weekend U.S. forces destroyed three Iranian tankers after the IRGC tried to attack a U.S. aircraft carrier and a destroyer.
Before Central Command’s statement, the Iranian news agency Tasnim, linked to the IRGC, had reported the attack on one of the tankers near Kharg. State broadcaster IRIB reported another vessel attacked at the port of Jask, slightly south of the Strait of Hormuz, also with no casualties, EFE reported.
In response to those attacks, the Revolutionary Guard warned that Kuwaiti and Bahraini tankers would be “targets of attacks,” and urged the crews of those vessels to leave the ports of both Arab countries immediately; both are U.S. allies and were accused by the IRGC of being complicit in Washington’s actions. Almost immediately, the IRGC said it had launched strikes on U.S. bases in Jordan and against two U.S. destroyers. Central Command has not confirmed those alleged strikes, but Jordan says it shot down 18 of 20 missiles launched by Iran.
“We are already witnessing a pattern of gradual escalation, both in terms of Iran’s now-confirmed repeated attempts to target U.S. warships and the increased quantity and quality of the missiles used to target U.S. bases,” Hamidreza Azizi of Crisis Group, a conflict-prevention organization, wrote on X.
As tensions intensify on the ground, the United States on Tuesday also stepped up economic pressure on Iran, sanctioning 36 entities and individuals tied to the aviation sector as part of what the Donald Trump administration has called Operation Economic Outcast, a package of direct and indirect sanctions and tariffs intended to isolate Tehran.
The sanctions in this case focus on 27 airlines still operating in Iran, on entities and individuals that provide support to the country’s main private carrier, Mahan Air, and on financial and supply channels for the sector.

items.title: Trump escalates trade war with ban on purchase of Canadian spirits and motorcycles
items.summary: The prohibition, which also includes dairy derivatives, will take effect on September 29
items.body_text:
Trump escalates trade war with ban on purchase of Canadian spirits and motorcycles
The prohibition, which also includes dairy derivatives, will take effect on September 29
The United States government will ban the import of a range of Canadian goods from the end of this month, in a new escalation of the trade war between the two countries. The announcement from the administration of Donald Trump came just hours after tariffs Ottawa imposed on U.S. products took effect as a reciprocal measure, following Washington’s imposition of 50% duties on a range of imports from its neighbor worth about $20 billion.
Among the products that will be barred are some Canadian spirits, motorcycles and certain dairy derivatives. The new measure will take effect in three weeks, on September 29, the White House said in a series of proclamations published on its website.
In a social media post hours earlier, Trump had lamented, as he has in recent weeks, what he considers a lack of Canadian “reciprocity” and warned he would order his administration to remove Canadian goods from lists of products authorized for import, after accusing the neighboring country of harming “American farmers and businesses.”
On Monday, the U.S. president had threatened to ban sales of planes from the private Canadian company Bombardier unless they were manufactured in the United States.
A senior U.S. administration official who spoke to reporters on condition of anonymity said the new ban aims to create “a level playing field” after Canada imposed its reciprocal tariffs on U.S. imports.
The official said his government has the authority to impose the ban under section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, passed in the midst of the Great Depression and which, he claims, authorizes the president to prohibit products from another country if that nation “does not end discriminatory conduct” against the United States. He also sought to downplay the episode, saying Washington remains open to possible negotiations and that the punished products were carefully chosen to avoid driving up prices and harming U.S. consumers.
November’s midterm elections, in which control of the Senate and the House of Representatives will be decided, are fast approaching amid a flurry of polls showing strong voter discontent with President Trump over the war with Iran and rising prices.
In a video shared on social media, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Tuesday urged a greater separation of Canada from its neighbor after decades in which the two countries maintained close diplomatic, economic, and military cooperation: Washington is Ottawa’s main trading partner. “We have everything we need to pivot and prosper,” Carney said, recalling that in January at the Davos conference he had declared the world order the United States founded after World War II dead and buried. “That pivot will come at a cost,” Carney acknowledged. “There’s always a cost to action. But it doesn’t come close to the cost of standing still.”
Canadian tariffs
Canadian tariffs range from 15% to 50% on U.S. imports and also cover furniture and electronic products. Ottawa said they would take effect on September 8 after negotiations between the two neighboring countries failed on the night of August 21 and the United States began to apply its duties.
Although the Supreme Court in June canceled a large portion of the broad tariffs Trump imposed last year, the current administration plans to impose a new round of duties on dozens of countries. The president — convinced that a trade deficit with a given country constitutes a scam, a position no one has managed to persuade him to review — favors that kind of tax as his preferred foreign policy tool. The new round, which could be announced in the coming days, is expected to be justified on the grounds that the affected countries have produced an excessive quantity of certain goods that they have sold to the United States, causing large deficits in bilateral trade balances.

items.title: Thousands quit working as part of public transport strike; Politicians visit strikers
items.summary: Several thousand workers laid down their work in public transport today, the trade union FNV said.
items.body_text:
Thousands quit working as part of public transport strike; Politicians visit strikers
Several thousand workers laid down their work in public transport today, the trade union FNV said. The trade unions organized a national strike against the Cabinet’s plans to cut certain social security budgets. The figure is an initial estimate from the Netherlands’ largest trade union. Other unions, including CNV, are also participating.
There are hardly any trains running due to the 24-hour strike. The NS stations were empty on Wednesday morning. Some areas also have no buses, trams or subways, like in The Hague, Rotterdam, and Amsterdam. Transport company Arriva tried to perform its services as normally as possible, but is also having to cancel a lot of buses.
The public transport strike is one of the trade unions’ actions against the social security cuts. The unions want the announced cuts to be completely abolished. There are also strikes at metal and construction companies this week. Harbor and port workers had already gone on strike.
Travel organization Rover has criticized the strikes. “The current strike has a purpose. The trade unions are trying to stand up for vulnerable people who are affected by the cuts,” said the organization’s director Daan Zieren to NOS. “But especially the vulnerable are isolated further by the mobility that is taken away from them today. That is why we are pleading for different ways of taking action.”
D66 parliamentary group leader Jan Paternotte and Jesse Klaver of Pro spoke with drivers and other public transport workers on strike in The Hague. Other politicians were also present, with SP member of parliament Sandra Beckerman shouting to the strikers that “only one solution is possible: strike strike strike!”
Paternotte said that he was disappointed with the plans to strike. “Watch for our plans to be released on Budget Day, then you can go on strike. But alright, it has happened today,” he said to NOS. Klaver, the leader of the largest opposition party, said he understands the strike. “The social security cuts need to be scrapped. It is currently at a standstill in The Hague, but I hope that the Cabinet chooses a direction.”
Reporting by ANP and NL Times

items.title: Former Ajax director Marc Overmars quits position at Royal Antwerp due to health issues
items.summary: Marc Overmars is quitting his position as technical director of Belgian club Royal Antwerp FC immediately.
items.body_text:
Former Ajax director Marc Overmars quits position at Royal Antwerp due to health issues
Marc Overmars is quitting his position as technical director of Belgian club Royal Antwerp FC immediately. The former Oranje international and Ajax director has health issues that require him to resign from the position, he has said on the club’s website.
“Unfortunately, the exhaustion and stress that have accumulated over the years came to a head last weekend. As you all know, my health has not been at its best. But now I feel very clearly today that I cannot handle this hectic, stressful professional life,” Overmars said. He had taken over as Antwerp’s technical director in 2022.
Overmars left his position at Ajax after accusations of transgressive behavior with female colleagues. This resulted in a global ban. He suffered a severe heart attack at the end of 2022.
The former Ajax, FC Barcelona, and Arsenal footballer said that he was already discussing a contract extension. “But my health is forcing me to be honest with myself and all the people around me. My energy is completely gone today. If I don’t listen to my body now, then doctors expect that the chance of a bad outcome is very high.”
Overmars added that in this case he had to make the drastic decision and stop his professional career for the time being. Overmars leaves a great legacy behind at Antwerp, where they won the Belgian league title and Belgian cup in 2023.
Reporting by ANP

items.title: Art and antique fair TEFAF to remain in Maastricht for another 10 years
items.summary: The art and antique fair TEFAF will remain in Maastricht for the next 10 years.
items.body_text:
Art and antique fair TEFAF to remain in Maastricht for another 10 years
The art and antique fair TEFAF will remain in Maastricht for the next 10 years. TEFAF, the municipality of Maastricht, the exhibition center MECC Maastricht, and the province of Limburg have agreed to this, the province said on Tuesday evening.
TEFAF has been held in Maastricht since 1988. The province describes it as “an event of great importance to the profile of our province that demonstrably generates substantial economic benefits.” In 2025, the fair attracted more than 41,000 visitors from 75 countries. There were 275 international gallery owners.
The current agreement with TEFAF was set to expire at the end of the next edition next year. “Alongside our fair in New York, Maastricht remains the place where we introduce the world to the highest level of art, design and antiques,” TEFAF chairman Boris Vervoordt said in the press release. He said he was pleased that new long-term agreements had been reached.
According to the newly released TEFAF Economic Impact Report conducted by Deloitte, the fair generates a total economic impact of €86.4 million across the Netherlands. Out of that total, €37.9 million directly goes into the city of Maastricht alone, heavily boosting local hotels, restaurants, transportation companies, and specialized art infrastructure services.
“We are grateful for their long-term vision, particularly in an international landscape where accessibility, infrastructure, hospitality, and international appeal are becoming ever more decisive,” said Maarten ten Holder, the Managing Director of TEFAF.
Reporting by ANP and NL Times

items.title: Non-EU doctors face €7,000 bill for Dutch medical test
items.summary: Doctors trained in non-EU countries will have to pay more than three times as much to sit the medical test...
items.body_text:
Non-EU doctors face €7,000 bill for Dutch medical test
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
Doctors trained in non-EU countries will have to pay more than three times as much to sit the medical test needed to practise in the Netherlands, under a draft regulation put forward by the health ministry.
The fee for the professional competence test will rise from €1,700 to €5,371.50 in March 2027, and to the full cost of running the test – just over €7,000 – a year later, the ministry says.
People already on the waiting list will have to pay the higher fee as the price is determined by the date of the exam, not the application. Non-EU trained dentists are also seeing their fees rise by almost double to help cover government expenses for organising the tests.
The ministry justifies the cost rises by saying that they will fund more test places. Currently only 72 doctors a year can take the test, which has caused waiting lists of up to two years. There are currently no places available.
Under a new contract with universities, up to 120 people will be able to take the test in 2027, cutting the waiting times by about a year.
More than 6,000 doctors and nurses from outside the EU came to the Netherlands in the past eight years, but only about 38% of doctors and 20% of nurses obtained the papers they need to work here, according to CIBG figures obtained by Trouw. Just over a third of dentists succeeded.
Candidates must first pass a Dutch language test at academic level before they can apply for the competence test, and most then work under supervision for several months before they can register.
“The route for international doctors is tough and takes a long time,” Paul Herfs of the association for foreign-trained doctors VBGA told Trouw. While waiting, he said, they cannot work as doctors, their Dutch language skills deteriorate and they can struggle with their mental health.
The number of non-EU dentists working in the Netherlands has doubled in five years, and the cabinet said in June it wants to steer refugees with medical qualifications into care jobs faster.

items.title: Setback for asset tax plan as BBB threatens to force senate vote
items.summary: The cabinet’s wealth tax reforms are in jeopardy after the farmers’ party BBB threatened to block them in the senate...
items.body_text:
Setback for asset tax plan as BBB threatens to force senate vote
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
The cabinet’s wealth tax reforms are in jeopardy after the farmers’ party BBB threatened to block them in the senate unless the coalition parties agree to a major overhaul.
MPs voted in favour of a new “box 3” tax on assets earlier this year, but the vote in the senate was postponed amid speculation that the centre-right coalition partners, VVD and CDA, were poised to vote against the plans in the upper house.
The cabinet wants to change the income tax system so that investors and savers are taxed on the growth of their assets each year, a system favoured by D66 and backed by VVD and CDA in the lower house.
But the two parties’ senators want to replace box 3 with a capital gains tax, which would be paid on the actual profit made from selling shares or other assets such as real estate.
Right-wing opposition parties, including the BBB and JA21, also favour this option, meaning the bill in its current form would almost certainly be voted down.
The BBB has said it will force a vote in the upper house unless finance minister Eelco Heinen withdraws the plan altogether, which would mean starting from scratch.
Withdraw or vote
“It can’t be up to the cabinet whether or not we examine a law in the Senate,” BBB senator Bart Kroon told the upper house’s finance committee. “Withdraw it or we’ll put it to the vote.”
Heinen had hoped to amend the bill as part of the current budget settlement so that it could be passed and enacted before 2028.
The finance minister has already torn up the plans once after the proposed new system attracted international criticism amid concern that investors would be forced to sell shares in order to pay tax on unrealised returns.
A new bill would not make it onto the statute book before 2029, costing the Dutch treasury an estimated €3 billion a year in lost revenue in the meantime.
The cabinet has been trying to reform the mechanism since the Supreme Court ruled in 2021 that the current system, which taxes assets based on a notional growth rate, breached European human rights laws.
Since then it has implemented a stopgap system that still taxes assets at a fictional rate but gives savers the option of declaring their actual growth rate instead. They can still pay the fictional rate if it works out lower.

items.title: Police step up campaign to stop illegal fireworks at New Year
items.summary: Dutch police say they will take a “zero tolerance” approach to illegal New Year fireworks in the first year after...
items.body_text:
Police step up campaign to stop illegal fireworks at New Year
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
Dutch police say they will take a “zero tolerance” approach to illegal New Year fireworks in the first year after a ban was imposed on most types of rockets and firecrackers.
A nationwide crackdown was launched after the ban came into force on August 1, including monitoring border crossings and checking vehicles that have been used in the past to import illegal firerworks.
“One of the conditions for introducing the fireworks ban was an extensive enforcement plan,” Ko Minderhoud, national fireworks co-ordinator for the Dutch police force, told the Telegraaf.
“We have a larger team than ever ready to go and we are starting earlier.”
MPs voted to ban all fireworks apart from the lightest category, F1, which includes sparklers and Roman candles, last year following a long campaign by doctors and emergency service workers.
The annual fireworks bonanza on December 31 is the busiest night of the year for police, ambulance and fire services.
Attacks on first responders in recent years prompted centre-right parties such as VVD and CDA to change their position and accept the need for a ban, even though many voters see New Year fireworks as a national tradition.
30% have fireworks stashed
The task facing the police is a daunting one. A survey by RTL found that nearly 30% of people who regularly set off fireworks said they still have some left over from before the ban, but just 4% are willing to hand them in.
View this post on Instagram
Just seven people turned up on the first day of an amnesty in Terneuzen on September 1 to take advantage of an offer to dispose of their fireworks anonymously without risking a fine.
The amnesty runs until October 9, with police buses touring the country to collect fireworks that are no longer permitted such as rockets and fountains.
Minderhoud said the illegal fireworks trade has been taken over in recent years by criminal gangs and increasingly resembles the drugs trade. “It’s become a sideline for classic organised criminals, because there’s a lot of money to be made,” he said.
“We see armed men transporting container loads. It was a different story a few years ago.”
He urged consumers to play their part by not buying illegal fireworks at New Year. “Set a good example and abide by the law,” he said.
“It’s also very dangerous. Look at the recent incidents at football matches. If you buy fireworks despite the ban, you’re getting involved in a murky world with very dangerous stuff.”

items.title: Poland secures further $4bn financing from US to buy American military equipment
items.summary: Poland's defence minister called it a "great honour", because such financing is "granted only to the best allies".
items.body_text:

Poland has signed an agreement for a further $4 billion (14.8 billion zloty) from the United States Foreign Military Financing (FMF) programme, which provides grants and loans to fund the purchase of American military equipment.
Defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz called the development a “great honour”, because FMF is “granted only to the best allies”. The agreement is not only “another important step in the modernisation of the Polish armed forces” but also “strengthens the strategic partnership between Poland and the US”.
The US embassy in Warsaw likewise hailed the agreement as “reaffirming the strength of the US-Poland partnership as we work together to strengthen NATO, deter aggression, and support peace and security in Europe”.
.@UnderSecT took part in the signing of a $4 billion Foreign Military Financing (FMF) loan guarantee—an important step in U.S.-Polish security cooperation. Poland’s significant investments in its defense capabilities and the U.S. defense industrial base reflect our shared… pic.twitter.com/Dz3huAp8pj
— US Embassy Warsaw (@USEmbassyWarsaw) September 9, 2026
Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Poland has embarked on an unprecedented military procurement spree, with its defence budget rising to the highest relative level in NATO.
Between 2021 and 2025, Poland was also the largest importer of arms in NATO. Around 44% of those purchases came from the US, including Abrams tanks, Patriot air defence batteries, and HIMARS rocket artillery.
The new agreement marks the sixth time Poland has received funds through FMF, for a total of almost $20 billion. Kosiniak-Kamysz said that the latest financing would be used to “accelerate the implementation of existing contracts, including for Apache helicopters”.
In 2024, Poland signed a $10 billion deal to buy 96 AH-64E Apache attack helicopters, along with a logistics and training package and a stockpile of ammunition and spare parts. It will make Poland the second-largest operator of Apaches in the world, after only the US itself.
Thomas DiNanno, the US under secretary of state for arms control and international security, said that the new agreement “signifies our commitment to assistance, but also Poland’s commitment to ensuring security, building defence capabilities, and ensuring the security of NATO’s eastern flank”.
“Poland is not only a trusted partner; it is not only an ally on the front line; it is a model ally of the United States,” he added, repeating recent remarks by US defence secretary Pete Hegseth.
The terms of the financing have not been revealed, but Marta Postuła, vice president of Poland’s national development bank, BGK, through which the funds will be channelled, said it was “on more favourable terms than the last two [FMF] loan guarantee agreements”.
This, she added, was “due to the subsidisation of a portion of the financing costs through a grant awarded for this purpose by the US government”.

items.title: “We remember where Germany in the hands of a far-right, pro-Russian party can lead,” says Polish FM
items.summary: The rise of the far-right AfD in Germany has been watched with particular concern in Poland.
items.body_text:
Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support.
Poland’s foreign minister has expressed concern over the rise of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party at a time when Germany is rapidly rearming – suggesting that it has echoes of the build-up to World War Two.
“We want Germany, under democratic leadership and as Europe’s largest economy, to play a strong role in ensuring our common security,” Radosław Sikorski told German newspaper Handelsblatt.
“But we remember all too well where a rearmed Germany in the hands of a far-right, pro-Russian party can lead – and that is precisely what the AfD represents,” he added.
Polens Außenminister Sikorski: „Wir wollen, dass Deutschland (…) eine starke Rolle bei der Sicherung unserer gemeinsamen Sicherheit spielt. Aber wir erinnern uns nur allzu gut daran, wohin ein wiederbewaffnetes Deutschland in den Händen einer rechtsextremen, prorussischen Partei führen kann (…)“
— Andreas Prause (@andreas-prause.eu) 8 September 2026 at 21:05
Poland was, on 1 September 1939, invaded by Nazi Germany, marking the start of World War Two and over five years of brutal occupation. The attack was launched in cooperation with the Soviet Union, which invaded Poland from the east two weeks later.
After Hitler was defeated, Germany had no major far-right party for decades. However, that has changed in recent years. In 2024, the AfD came first in the Thuringian state election, with 33% of the vote. Last Sunday, it won in Saxony-Anhalt, with 44%.
The party also came second in the federal elections of 2025, with 21%, making it the main national opposition. Opinion polls now show that the AfD is the most popular party nationally, with support of around 28%, well ahead of Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s Christian Democratic Union (CDU), on 21%.
The AfD’s growth has been watched with particular concern in Poland, a country that suffered enormously under Nazi-German occupation. Some senior AfD figures have sought to downplay the significance of the Nazi era.
In 2025, when the German parliament approved plans for a memorial in Berlin to Polish victims of World War Two, the AfD was the only party not to vote in favour.
The AfD’s sympathy towards and links with Russia have caused further disquiet in Poland. Last year, AfD co-leader Tino Chrupalla said he “does not see any current threat to Germany from Russia” and that, in fact, “Poland could also be a threat to us”.
This year, another senior AfD figure, Kay Gottschalk, called for Poland to pay his country €1.3 billion as reparations for its “complicity” in the sabotage of the Nord Stream gas pipelines that used to bring Russian gas to Germany through the Baltic Sea but were damaged by explosions in 2022.
Germany’s parliament has passed a motion calling on the government to establish a permanent memorial in Berlin to Polish victims of the German-Nazi occupation.

items.title: Station Narva draws record 5,766 visitors for 10th edition
items.summary: The weekend's Station Narva festival attracted nearly 6,000 visitors, a record figure in the decade the event has been running.
items.body_text:
Station Narva draws record 5,766 visitors for 10th edition
The weekend's Station Narva festival attracted nearly 6,000 visitors, a record figure in the decade the event has been running.
The music and city festival, held from Thursday, September 3 to Sunday, September 6, brought 5,766 visitors, and founder and director Helen Sildna said attendance confirms that Station Narva has found a place in the hearts of its audience.
"The city of Narva and the people of Ida-Viru County have embraced us. It brings our team heartfelt joy to see such different people spending time together at the festival – from young people to seniors, from across Estonia and Europe. That is exactly our wish and aim: to create a cultural event that brings people together and unites, motivates and encourages them. We are already starting work today on the tenth Station Narva," Sildna said.
Culture Minister Heidy Purga (Reform), who opened the festival's music program, said Station Narva is evidence of how music brings people together and opens the city to new perspectives.
"You may leave here with a new favorite song, a new friendship or a reason to return to Narva. What moved me most this year was Skoone's concert and meeting local young people, whose energy and desire to connect their creativity with their hometown and Station Narva show that this festival has a future in Narva that is very much its own and very much needed," Purga said.
Musical headliners included British trip‑hop pioneer and Station Narva regular Tricky, Icelandic electronic pop act GusGus and Estonian artists spanning several generations and genres, among them folk‑pop band Sadu, veteran punk act Propeller and Narva native and 2023 Eurovision representative Alika, who was also celebrating her birthday.
Concerts mainly took place at the Narva Museum inside the historic Hermann Castle, and at the Ro‑Ro club.
Free daytime concerts featured actor and solo artist Mihkel Kuusk as well as other local and Estonian acts, art installations and more.
Next year's Station Narva is the 10th edition and is set to run over the same weekend, September 2‑5, 2027.

items.title: Estonian PM to officially offer former EDF commander the post of defense minister
items.summary: Prime Minister Kristen Michal will ask former Estonian Defense Forces commander Martin Herem to become the new defense minister.
items.body_text:
Estonian PM to officially offer former EDF commander the post of defense minister
Prime Minister Kristen Michal will ask former Estonian Defense Forces commander Martin Herem to become the new defense minister.
According to Michal, Herem's experience and knowledge of what needs to be improved within the Ministry of Defense's area of responsibility make him a strong candidate. He added that Herem will most likely become the new defense minister.
It was previously reported that Prime Minister Michal had privately offered Herem the position of defense minister, but Herem himself has not publicly accepted the offer. It is now known that the Reform Party board will approve Herem's candidacy at its meeting on Tuesday.
According to Michal, Herem is demanding that defense spending remain at 5 percent. "His message to me, as well as to others who have asked him, has been that the Russian threat is real and must be addressed," he added.
The Reform Party will first wait for Herem's response on whether he will take up the ministerial post, after which it will begin making offers to other candidates as well.
According to the prime minister, Herem needs political support to carry out various reforms, including an overhaul of the defense sector. "The problems that exist there need to be resolved," Michal said.
Herem's answer needed first
The Reform Party will first wait for Herem's response on whether he will take up the ministerial post, after which it will approach other candidates. Michal named Marko Mihkelson, Alar Laneman, Kalle Laanet, Eerik-Niiles Kross, Kristo Enn Vaga and Mati Raidma as other possible choices.
Asked whether the dismissal of Ministry of Defense Permanent Secretary Kaimo Kuusk is also an important issue for Herem, Michal said the former commander of the Estonian Defense Forces would be joining the ministry primarily to put the defense sector in order.
"In that sense, Kuusk's message has been honorable: He was the first to raise his hand and say that he takes responsibility. Hopefully, the government can dismiss him tomorrow and begin, so to speak, cleaning up or putting the ministry in order," Michal said.
Martin Herem has previously said that joining the Reform Party cannot be a prerequisite or condition of taking up the ministerial post.
Postimees wrote on Wednesday that Martin Herem has decided to accept the offer to become defense minister.
Currently on vacation abroad, Herem told Postimees that he will attend next Thursday's Reform Party board meeting, adding, "I plan to make it a yes answer." Herem also said he doesn't yet know who will make up his team as he hasn't had the chance to even speak to potential candidates.
It emerged on Wednesday that Energy and Environment Minister Andres Sutt, a member of the Reform Party, will step down as minister. "Since we're already reshuffling the Cabinet, it makes sense to change ministers now as well," Michal said. The prime minister will look for a new minister both within and outside the party.
The article was updated to add comments from Martin Herem.
--
Editor: Merilin Leetna, Marcus Turovski

items.title: Rail Baltica trains procurement fails
items.summary: A joint procurement by Baltic passenger rail operators Elron, Vivi and LTG Link for Rail Baltica regional trains failed to receive any compliant bids by the deadline.
items.body_text:
Rail Baltica trains procurement fails
A joint procurement by Baltic passenger rail operators Elron, Vivi and LTG Link for Rail Baltica regional trains failed to receive any compliant bids by the deadline.
"Although there was strong interest in the procurement among train manufacturers and six different manufacturers registered for the tender, no compliant bids for the joint procurement of Rail Baltica regional trains were received by the deadline," said Elron management board member Märt Ehrenpreis.
"During the procurement process, two train manufacturers continued to submit questions and comments regarding the technical requirements and contract terms until the final days. After reviewing the feedback, we will clarify the procurement documents and launch a new tender. Since all parties have already completed the bulk of the work on the procurement, we expect the new tender process to take less time," Ehrenpreis said.
The Rail Baltica regional trains to be procured will operate on the 1,435-millimeter-gauge infrastructure currently under construction and will enable faster, more comfortable and more environmentally friendly travel. The Estonian, Latvian and Lithuanian passenger rail operators plan to procure up to 20 regional trains in total, suitable for the European standard gauge of 1,435 millimeters and capable of reaching a maximum speed of 200 kilometers per hour.
"Estonia plans to purchase five trains, with an option to increase the order to seven," Ehrenpreis said. "Under the procurement, Latvia can purchase up to five trains and Lithuania up to eight."
The tender for the purchase of regional trains suitable for the 1,435-millimeter track gauge was launched on March 18. Bids could be submitted until noon on September 8.
The procurement is being conducted jointly by the Baltic passenger rail operators Elron, Vivi and LTG Link to ensure compatibility with Rail Baltica infrastructure and seamless cross-border services.
--

items.title: Serbia’s Vucic Calls Early Parliamentary Elections for October 25
items.summary: President sets October 25 election date, saying Serbia needs an end to a year-and-a-half of 'turbulence' - referring to student-led protests that have rocked the country.
items.body_text:
Serbia’s Vucic Calls Early Parliamentary Elections for October 25
Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic on Tuesday set a date for early parliamentary elections on October 25, signing a decree dissolving parliament and the decision calling the elections – in which he is expected to run for prime minister, facing down a strong challenge from opponents.
“We need election results that will clearly demonstrate and determine the will of the citizens as to where, in what direction, and along which path Serbia is heading,” he said, adding that Serbia has been enduring “turbulence for more than a year and a half”.
Student-led protests have gripped the country since November 2024, sparked by the collapse of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad that left 16 people dead, sparking nationwide outrage over alleged official corruption and negligence. The protests have posed the strongest challenge to Vucic’s Serbian Progressive Party since it came to power in 2012.
Vucic claimed the “turbulence” in society was not merely the result of “conflicts between political parties or political actors here in Serbia” but also involved “significant interference by foreign powers”. He and his Progressive Party have often claimed that foreign states, including European countries, have been involved in supporting or inciting the student-led protests.
In his comments on Tuesday, however, he also insisted that Serbia, an EU candidate state, had chosen “a good European path, while [also] preserving traditional friendships, national pride, and dignity” – referencing Belgrade’s continued friendly relationship with Russia.
As one of the reasons for calling early elections, Vucic cited the organisation of the high-profile international EXPO 2027 exhibition, which will be held in Belgrade starting in May next year.
“If it were not for these tensions, if it were not for these political disagreements and conflicts, we certainly would not need [elections]. But any delay would jeopardise both EXPO and the survival of democracy as the best form of political system in our country,” he said.
On Monday, Prime Minister Djuro Macut proposed the dissolution of parliament, which was adopted by the government and sent to the President as part of the official procedure.
Many experts see the upcoming elections as the most challenging for Vucic and his party since 2012. The main opponent this time is Student List, made by the students who have been protesting. Its official candidates have been chosen by student groups whose names haven’t been published yet.
“The elections have been called after 492 days. It’s time for victory,” student organising group Students Blockade wrote on X on Tuesday. It was alluding to May 2025, when it first publicly demanded early elections.
Last Saturday, the Main Board of the Progressive Party named Vucic as their candidate for prime minister and as first on the electoral list “Aleksandar Vucic – United Serbia” at the upcoming elections.
At the December 2023 elections, the Progressive Party won 46.75 per cent of the votes, while the largest opposition coalition, Serbia against Violence, won 23.66 per cent. The Progressive Party’s junior partner, the Socialist Party of Serbia, SPS, won 6.55 per cent.

items.title: Montenegro Opposition Moves to Oust Speaker for Mladic Condolences
items.summary: Opposition pushes for removal of Andrija Mandic as speaker of parliament after he expressed public condolences following death of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic.
items.body_text:
Montenegro Opposition Moves to Oust Speaker for Mladic Condolences
This post is also available in this language: Shqip
Montenegro’s main opposition party has moved to oust Speaker of Parliament Andrija Mandic over his public condolences following the death of the convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic, media reported on Wednesday.
The initiative led by the Democratic Party of Socialists, DPS, was signed by 35 of the chamber’s 81 lawmakers, while 29 opposition MPs submitted a request for an extraordinary session on September 24 to debate Mandic’s dismissal.
The proposal says the speaker’s position carries “special political and institutional responsibility” and an obligation to safeguard the reputation and integrity of parliament, which represents all citizens.
Mandic publicly expressed condolences following the death on August 27 of Mladic, who was convicted by the UN war crimes tribunal in The Hague of genocide, crimes against humanity and other war crimes. He died serving his sentence.
The DPS said expressing sorrow for a convicted war criminal, particularly someone convicted of the 1995 genocide in Srebrenica, is incompatible with the responsibilities of the speaker and Montenegro’s obligation to respect international court rulings and good neighbourly relations.
The proposal denies that Mandic expressed his condolences in a personal or party capacity, saying his institutional responsibility remains because he simultaneously holds the position of speaker.
The document cites critical reactions to the funeral from the European Commission and neighbouring Croatia, which condemned the glorification of war criminals and Mandic’s expression of condolences as incompatible with European Union values.
“When the actions of the speaker of parliament of a candidate country produce such reactions from EU institutions and a neighbouring member state, they can no longer be presented as a matter of his personal or party convictions,” the proposal says.
The DPS also argues that the episode is not isolated but forms part of a broader pattern in Mandic’s exercise of the speaker’s office.
The proposal also raises concerns about his alleged use of the speaker’s office to promote political and ideological positions.
The proposal recalls that Montenegro is entering a decisive phase of its EU integration process and that membership requires more than meeting technical conditions, including a clear commitment to European values, confronting the past, respecting international court judgments and maintaining good-neighbourly relations.
“We believe that the speaker’s latest action has crossed the line beyond which the question of his responsibility can no longer be relativised by the need to preserve the parliamentary majority or political stability,” the proposal says.
The ruling coalition’s three main groups, Prime Minister Milojko Spajic’s Europe Now Movement, the Democrats and the New Serb Democracy, which together hold 41 seats in the 81-member parliament, said they will not support the opposition initiative.
But parties representing Montenegro’s Bosniak and ethnic Albanian communities, which are also part of the governing coalition, have announced they will back the motion.
An absolute majority of all 81 lawmakers is not required to dismiss Mandic. The motion can pass with a majority of lawmakers present at the session, provided that at least half of all MPs are present.
Montenegro’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs this week also expressed concern about the glorification of Mladic during the recent commemorations of his death.
“It is our obligation to preserve the dignity and memory of the victims, to preserve the truth about crimes and individual responsibility for them, and to resolutely oppose any attempt to deny genocide, war crimes and other serious violations of international humanitarian law,” the Montenegrin ministry said in a statement on Tuesday.

items.title: Serbia, Bosnian Serbs Slate Sarajevo’s Expulsion of Diplomats over Mladic
items.summary: Bosnia's expulsion of two Serbian embassy staff, in response to the honours given to Ratko Mladic's funeral, draws angry response from Serbia and Bosnian Serb officials – who questioned its legitimacy.
items.body_text:
Serbia, Bosnian Serbs Slate Sarajevo’s Expulsion of Diplomats over Mladic
The Serbian embassy in Sarajevo. Photo: Serbian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. 
Serbia’s Foreign Ministry on Tuesday condemned the expulsion of two of its diplomats from Bosnia and Herzegovina as “yet another unconstructive move” that serves neither good-neighbourly relations, regional stability, nor the easing of political tensions.
It said Bosnia’s Foreign Minister, Elmedin Konakovic, “continues to resort to escalation and uses extremely difficult and painful issues from our shared past as an instrument of day-to-day politics and an election campaign”, adding that “such issues require responsibility and serious dialogue, rather than political instrumentalisation and unilateral moves that further deepen divisions.”
The ministry said Serbia will “examine all legal and political aspects of the announced decisions, including the issue of jurisdiction and the procedures for adopting them,” as well as their consequences for diplomatic relations.
On Tuesday, Konakovic announced the expulsion of two members of the Serbian embassy in Sarajevo after Serbia hosted the funeral with military honours of the convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladic in Belgrade.
Konakovic said Serbian military attache Milan Dulanovic and Danko Maksimovic, an adviser to Serbia’s BIA intelligence service, were personae non grata and had 48 hours to leave Bosnia.
Officials in Bosnia’s mainly Serb Republika Srpska entity, also condemned the move and challenged its legality.
Republika Srpska Justice Minister Goran Selak insisted such foreign policy decisions fall under the authority of Bosnia’s tripartite state presidency, while the Foreign Ministry merely carries out adopted policy – which he said Konakovic “would have to know” before making moves that are “unconstitutional and illegal.”
He said the expulsion order “can hardly even be called a decision,” since such a decision must have grounding in the constitution and law. “This looks more like a pre-election pamphlet than a serious act of an institution,” Selak said, referring to upcoming national elections next month.
Selak said Konakovic has the right to his opinions, “including personal antipathy toward Serbia”, but not to present them as the country’s position or speak for Republika Srpska, adding that “Serbia is Republika Srpska’s most important partner”.
The Serb member of Bosnia’s three-member state presidency, Zeljka Cvijanovic, said Konakovic “cannot determine what Bosnia and Herzegovina is, or dictate to Serbia”. She claimed one of the two embassy staff had already left Bosnia after his mandate expired.
Konakovic based the decision on a 2004 rulebook of the state presidency, Under it, only the presidency can expel heads of diplomatic missions but the foreign minister can expel other embassy staff for cases including interference in internal affairs, espionage, or insulting statements.

items.title: Lake Balaton to Host Spectacular International Kite Festival
items.summary: From September 18 to 20, Zamárdi on the southern shore of Lake Balaton will become a colorful open-air showcase where art takes to the skies. The International Kite Festival “Égenjáró” (“Sky Traveler”) returns for its second edition, offering visitors a free cultural and family event featuring spectacular kites, aerial artworks, and hands-on activities. At the […] The post Lake Balaton to Host Spectacular International Kite Festival appeared first on Hungary Today.
items.body_text:
The ELTE Botanical Garden will showcase rare Mexican cacti and succulents.Continue reading
From September 18 to 20, Zamárdi on the southern shore of Lake Balaton will become a colorful open-air showcase where art takes to the skies. The International Kite Festival “Égenjáró” (“Sky Traveler”) returns for its second edition, offering visitors a free cultural and family event featuring spectacular kites, aerial artworks, and hands-on activities.
At the local free beach and the “ZAM! Kultúrbuborék” cultural center, professional Hungarian kite flyers will meet around 20 artists from five countries. The focus will go beyond traditional flying kites.
Floating sculptures, unconventional flying constructions, and rare one-of-a-kind creations will shape the panorama above the “Hungarian Sea.”
Weather permitting, the festival will kick off with an atmospheric night-flying display on the evening of September 18. The weekend program features a wide range of hands-on activities for visitors of all ages:
- Kite-building workshops: Instructors and students from the Moholy-Nagy University of Art and Design (MOME) will lead workshops where participants can design and build their own kites and other flying creations.
- Daytime demonstrations: Professional kite flyers will showcase impressive flight maneuvers and artistic aerial installations.
- Additional activities: Alongside the action in the sky, the program will feature board game stations and outdoor yoga by the lakeshore.
The festival will wrap up with a spectacular “group picture in the sky,” as numerous kites and other creations take flight simultaneously.
A special focus of the festival will be the Hungarian children’s author Éva Janikovszky (1926–2003), whose 100th birthday would have been celebrated in 2026. Inspired by her well-known work “Égig érő fű” (“That Lovely Green Grass”), a specially designed giant installation will take to the skies several times during the festival. An exhibition by the long-established Móra Publishing House will also open at the cultural center, celebrating the work of the author and her longtime illustrator, László Réber. On Saturday, September 19, the awards ceremony for an accompanying creative competition for children will also take place.
The event blurs the line between a toy and fine art, the organizers noted. Kite building sparks creativity, encouraging participants to experiment with different designs and try new ideas, while flying their creations offers a shared sense of accomplishment.
Via MTI, Featured image: Pexels

items.summary: There were warning signs, but the company was still hiring this summer. The German automotive company had been operating in Győr, northwestern Hungary, for 30 years, but now WKW is shutting down. Exactly what caused the closure is still difficult to determine, Világgazdaság writes. What had been rumored for days is now official. Just a […] The post German Company to Close Győr Plant That Supplied Audi appeared first on Hungary Today.
items.body_text:
The automaker has denied the reported job-cutting plans at its plant in Győr.Continue reading
There were warning signs, but the company was still hiring this summer. The German automotive company had been operating in Győr, northwestern Hungary, for 30 years, but now WKW is shutting down. Exactly what caused the closure is still difficult to determine, Világgazdaság writes.
What had been rumored for days is now official. Just a few minutes ago, the mayor of Győr announced on social media that the WKW plant will close and its employees will be laid off.
Bence Pintér wrote: “On September 7, I received the sad news that the parent company of WKW, a multinational automotive company, has decided that due to the impact of the economic situation, WKW Hungária Kft. will cease its operations in Győr by the end of the year, and the Hungarian company will be dissolved without a legal successor. I will do my best over the coming days to gather as much information as possible about the situation.”
The mayor added that he had spoken with Zoltán László, vice president of the Vasas Trade Union, and that they would begin reviewing what options are available and what assistance they can provide to the employees.
According to reports, around 500 jobs will be lost as a result of the closure.
Kisalföld reports that there had been problems at WKW Hungária, located in the Industrial Park, for some time. Last year, the plant’s employees even went on strike. The facility could not be saved or sold, despite the fact that the German owner had invested a substantial amount of money in it not long ago.
WKW’s premium automotive trim manufacturing operation is now shutting down for good. One of the employees told the newspaper that WKW Hungária Kft. management informed workers on Monday at 1 p.m., 2 p.m., and 10 p.m. that WKW’s German parent company, citing restructuring and declining orders, would dissolve the Győr-based company without a legal successor on December 31.
The plant manufactures trim for premium vehicles such as Audi, Mercedes-Benz, Jaguar, and Porsche.
Management said it would proceed in accordance with the law and that all employees would be paid everything they are owed. In addition, workers will receive an extra one or two months of retention pay on top of their regular severance packages.
What is particularly concerning is that the closure of the WKW plant may be just one domino in a larger chain reaction. Union sources say
the current plant closure is part of a broader process, and several other companies in the automotive industry are also reportedly imposing hiring freezes and letting go of employees with fixed-term contracts.
For the full picture, it is worth noting that the press was already reporting problems at WKW’s Hungarian subsidiary in February of last year. Employees at WKW Hungária Kft. in Győr held a protest over what they considered unfavorable measures imposed by the company. They objected to unilateral decisions concerning wage increases and changes to the bonus system. At the time, the employees and company management managed to reach an agreement.
Publicly available company records show that WKW accumulated after-tax losses of HUF 1.818 billion (EUR 5 million / EUR 1=HUF 364) in 2023, HUF 5.898 billion in 2024, and HUF 6.008 billion last year. The company employed 465 people last year. WKW Hungária Kft. has been operating in Győr for nearly three decades.
Just a few years ago, the company carried out significant investments at the site. At the time, the German owner invested approximately EUR 85 million in the Győr plant over a two-year period, increasing its production area from 8,000 to 24,000 square meters. At the same time, the company’s financial situation has deteriorated significantly in recent years. Yet despite the fact that the plant closure officially became known in September, WKW Hungária was still looking to hire new employees for its Győr facility as recently as this summer. items.title: A Kreml az orosz diplomaták kiutasítása ellenére nyitott kapcsolatai fejlesztésére Magyarországgal
items.summary: Putyin szóvivője szerint ők nem hívei annak, hogy kárt okozzanak az orosz–magyar kapcsolatok értékes örökségében.
items.body_text:
A Kreml az orosz diplomaták kiutasítása ellenére nyitott kapcsolatai fejlesztésére Magyarországgal
Oroszország megfelelő választ fog adni arra, hogy Magyarország kiutasított tíz orosz diplomatát – közölte Dmitrij Peszkov, az orosz elnök sajtótitkára szerdán Moszkvában. Peszkov úgy fogalmazott: „Ami konkrétan ezt a döntést illeti, természetesen megfelelő válasz fog születni rá, ezek a lépések nem maradnak válasz nélkül.”
Szerinte Magyarország barátságtalan lépései kétségkívül negatívan hatnak majd, és nem lehet, hogy ne járjanak negatív következményekkel a kétoldalú orosz–magyar kapcsolatok egészére nézve. „Nyitottak vagyunk kapcsolataink további fejlesztésére. Ez érdekünkben áll, és nem vagyunk hívei annak, hogy bármilyen kárt okozzunk az orosz–magyar kétoldalú kapcsolataink, mondjuk úgy, értékes örökségében és tapasztalataiban.”
Kedden derült ki, hogy a Külügyminisztérium kiutasította Magyarországról az orosz nagykövetség 10 munkatársát is. Orbán Anita külügyminiszter ugyanakkor azt mondta, ez nem jelenti az Oroszországgal fennálló diplomáciai kapcsolatok megszakítását, Magyarország továbbra is fenn kívánja tartani a szükséges párbeszédet a kölcsönös tisztelet és a szabályok betartása mellett. Rácz András, a Magyar Külügyi Intézet vezérigazgató-helyettese azt nyilatkozta, a külügyminiszter nyilatkozatából a diplomáciai nyelvezet szabályai szerint az következik, hogy a Magyarországról kiutasított tíz orosz diplomata valójában diplomáciai fedésben dolgozott, és hírszerzői tevékenységet folytatott.
A bejelentés üzenet lehet Oroszországnak arról, hogy új időszak jön, többé Magyarország nem lesz kíméletes az orosz hírszerzőkkel. De az is elképzelhető, hogy ez nem Moszkvának, hanem inkább azoknak a nyugati szövetségeseknek és partnereknek szól, akik már jó ideje nem bíztak a magyarokban.
Az orosz külügyminisztérium szóvivője a hírre reagálva „kemény és fájdalmas” választ ígért. „Először is, mi ugyanezt fogjuk tenni. De Magyarország döntése a közös gazdasági projektek csökkenéséhez is vezethet Oroszországgal” – nyilatkozta az orosz TASZSZ hírügynökségnek Alekszej Csepa, az Állami Duma Nemzetközi Ügyek Bizottságának alelnöke.

items.title: Havasi Bertalan azt állítja, hogy Leslie Mandoki tőle kért kommunikációs tanácsokat a Telex megkeresése után
items.summary: A Fidesz kommunikációs igazgatóját ezért is lepte meg, hogy Mandoki lapunknak azt írta, hálás a kormányváltásért.
items.body_text:
Havasi Bertalan azt állítja, hogy Leslie Mandoki tőle kért kommunikációs tanácsokat a Telex megkeresése után
Meglepte Havasi Bertalant, hogy Leslie Mandoki lapunknak azt írta, ő nem sorolná be magát orbánistának, „és hálás azért, hogy a kormányváltás után Magyarország visszakerült a szabad Európába.”
A 24.hu cikkünk után kereste meg a Fidesz kommunikációs igazgatóját, aki meglepő választ adott.
„Múlt szerdán Leslie barátom felhívott, a Telex megkeresése kapcsán kommunikációs tanácsokat kért, negyed órát beszélgettünk”
– írta a lapnak Havasi, majd hozzátette, az ott elhangzottak alapján kissé meglepte Mandoki nyilatkozata, „de ő egy világhírű, nagy formátumú művész-személyiség; ki vagyok én, hogy kritizáljam a véleményét és a meggyőződését, akármi legyen is az.”
Havasi állításaival kapcsolatban megkerestük Leslie Mandoki menedzsmentjét. Arra voltunk kíváncsiak, hogy a zenész valóban felkereste-e Havasit kérdéseink után, és ha igen miért tett így, illetve pontosan melyik kérdésünkkel kapcsolatban volt szüksége tanácsra. Ha választ kapunk, beszámolunk róla.
A magyar származású, Németországban élő zenészt eredetileg azért kerestük meg, mert birtokunkba jutott néhány dokumentum, amelyek szerint Orbán Viktor kérésére és a miniszterelnöki protokollkeret terhére rendszeresen reptéri kormányváró és bérelt luxusautó várta Budapesten. A zenész a dokumentumok alapján az elmúlt két évben több tízmillió forint értékben kapott a magyar államtól olyan kényelmi szolgáltatásokat, amelyek leginkább miniszterelnököknek vagy más, magas rangú diplomatáknak járnak.
Mikor azonban erről érdeklődtünk, a NER egyik kedvenc zenészének tartott Mandoki azt állította, valójában évek óta nem értett egyet az Orbán-kormány bizonyos álláspontjaival, és hálás azért, hogy a kormányváltás után Magyarország visszakerült a szabad Európába. Részletek itt.

items.title: Azonnali hatállyal felmentették az állami felszámolócég felügyelőbizottsági elnökét
items.summary: A tulajdonos, a Magyar Nemzeti Vagyonkezelő döntött.
items.body_text:
Azonnali hatállyal felmentették az állami felszámolócég felügyelőbizottsági elnökét
Azonnali hatállyal felmentették a Nemzeti Reorganizációs Nonprofit Kft. (NRN) állami felszámolótársaság felügyelőbizottsági elnökét, Mike Ferencet, a döntést tulajdonosként a Magyar Nemzeti Vagyonkezelő (MNV) hozta meg – írja a HVG a birtokába került dokumentum alapján, amelyet Körtvélyessy Zsolt, az MNV társaságokért felelős igazgatója írt alá.
Az állami felszámoló operatív vezetése Mike felmentése után egyelőre a helyén maradt, írja a lap. Az ügyben kerestük az MNV-t, ha válaszolnak, beszámolunk róla.
Az állami felszámoló cég adta el négy évvel ezelőtt a tőzsdén jegyzett Waberer's egyötöd részét Tiborcz István cégcsoportjának, a BDPST-nek. Az NRN már korábban, a Quaestor 2015-ös bebukásakor is feltűnt, amikor végelszámolóként működött közre.
A HVG megjegyzi, hogy a felmentés gyakorlatilag egyidőben történt azzal, hogy a kormány kiemeltté nyilvánította a Bayer Construct csődeljárását. Ez azután indult, hogy a Magyar Péter vezette új kormány augusztusban elállt a Bosnyák téri irodakomplexum megvásárlásától, és visszakérik a cserébe kifizetett 300 milliárd forintot a Bayer-csoporttól. Az ügyletre még 2023-ban kötött előszerződést Orbán Viktor kormánya.
A döntés miatt az irodaházak most üresen állnak, a negyedet felépítő projektcég és a Bayer Construct pedig csődeljárást kért maga ellen.

items.body_text:
Prague Unemployment Reaches 4% with 40,509 Job Seekers
Prague Morning
Unemployment in Prague rises to 4% at the end of August, with 40,509 people registered as job seekers at the Labour Office.
The figure was 2.1% higher than in July and 15.7% higher than a year earlier.
Despite the increase, Prague continued to record the lowest unemployment rate among Czechia’s regions. The national unemployment rate stood at 5% at the end of August.
More people registered as job seekers
A total of 5,368 people registered with the Prague Labour Office in August. That was 133 fewer than in July but 1,033 more than in August 2025.
At the end of August, Prague had 37,811 people considered reachable for employment. This category covers people aged 15 to 64 who are not temporarily unable to work and are not taking part in retraining.
The number of reachable job seekers increased by 822 compared with July and by 5,475 compared with the same month last year.
Women accounted for 55.2% of all registered job seekers, with 22,378 women listed in the Labour Office records.
More than 22,000 vacancies remain available
Employers in Prague had 22,519 registered vacancies at the end of August. That was 708 fewer positions than in July and 565 fewer than a year earlier.
There were an average of 1.8 registered job seekers for every vacancy.
Of the total number of registered vacancies, 1,676 were not marked as positions available to foreign workers. Employers could recruit workers from abroad for a further 20,843 positions.
Construction, accommodation and food services, and wholesale and retail were among the sectors with the largest number of vacancies.

items.body_text:
AIGEL to Celebrate 10th Anniversary with Prague Concert
Prague Morning
On October 21, electronic duo AIGEL will perform at Futurum Music Bar in Prague as part of a special concert marking the band’s 10th anniversary.
AIGEL was formed by Tatar poet and singer Aigel Gaisina and St. Petersburg producer Ilya Baramiya. Over the past decade, the duo has developed a distinctive sound combining electronic music, trip-hop and psychedelic influences.
Their music crosses linguistic and cultural boundaries, with songs performed in Russian, Tatar, English and German.
AIGEL gained international attention with the viral tracks “Tatarin” and “Pyyala.” The latter topped streaming charts in 25 countries and reached No. 1 on the global Shazam chart.
Over 10 years, the duo has released five albums and dozens of singles. They have also received a Cannes Lion for the music video “You’re Born” and toured extensively across Europe and beyond.
Now based in Europe, AIGEL is preparing a special anniversary show in Prague, combining the duo’s electronic sound with Gaisina’s distinctive and expressive vocals.
The concert will take place on October 21 at Futurum Music Bar.

items.body_text:
Prague to Add 51 New Trams Next Year as Network Expands
Prague Morning
Prague is set to receive 51 new trams next year as the city expands its tram network and begins replacing some of its oldest vehicles.
The Prague Public Transport Company (DPP) has ordered another 25 Škoda 52T trams under an existing framework agreement with Škoda Transportation.
Each tram costs CZK 82.5 million, including CZK 40 million in European subsidies. Prague has now committed to buying 71 of the new vehicles in three separate orders.
The first 20 Škoda 52T trams entered regular service in Prague last year. Another batch is being delivered this year, while the latest orders will continue into 2027.
The newest order for 25 additional trams is due to be completed by December 3 next year.
The new vehicles are needed not only because Prague is building new tram lines but also because the existing fleet needs to be renewed. Some of the oldest trams still in operation are the T3M models, while a large part of the fleet consists of reconstructed T3R.P and T3R.PV vehicles and their derivatives.
Replacing older models with a smaller number of standardised tram types should also reduce maintenance and servicing costs, according to the deputy mayor. The new trams are expected to remain in service for around 20 to 30 years, compared with approximately 15 years for buses.
The Škoda 52T is 32 metres long and 2.5 metres wide and can carry up to 243 passengers. Of these, 173 can travel standing. The tram therefore offers almost 16 percent more capacity than Prague’s Škoda 15T trams.
The maximum operating speed is 70 kilometres per hour.
The 52T was designed specifically for Prague’s tram network, including sections with narrow and sharply curved tracks. This allows the vehicles to operate on existing routes without requiring major changes to the infrastructure.
