The government will provide a subsidy of 50,000 baht per household for solar installations, which can be installed either on rooftops or on the ground. The scheme is initially expected to cover 1 million households, while the Interior Ministry is considering expanding the target to 1.5 million.
Mr Ekniti said the key objective of the programme is to turn people from electricity consumers into electricity producers, enabling them to sell surplus power back to the grid.
“People who do not have a lump sum to invest do not need to worry,” said he said. “We will bring state-owned financial institutions, including the Government Savings Bank, Government Housing Bank and Bank for Agriculture and Agricultural Cooperatives into the programme to support the initial investment.
“Electricity authorities will purchase the electricity generated and use the resulting revenue (from reselling electricity) to deduct repayments to the financial institutions, meaning people may not have to put up any investment themselves,” he said. (Story continues below)
A technician installs rooftop solar panels. (Photo: Gunkul)
B1,000 a month earned
Mr Ekniti said preliminary estimates showed that a household installing a 5-kilowatt system and using relatively little electricity could earn about 1,000 baht a month by selling surplus electricity to power utilities.
The system could generate income throughout the solar panels’ lifespan of 25-30 years. For households with high electricity consumption, the installation could result in substantial savings on electricity bills, he said.
A key condition for participation is that there must be one electricity meter owner per entitlement. The subsidy will only be paid after electricity authorities have completed the system connection to prevent fraud and false claims.
The metropolitan and provincial electricity authorities are also preparing a major infrastructure upgrade, including the introduction of smart meters, development of a smart grid, expansion of transmission lines and installation of battery energy storage systems.
Aside from generating income for households, the scheme is also intended to create jobs and support domestic industries, Mr Ekniti said.
The government will also exempt tax on some solar panel part imports, he added. (Story continues below)
Consumer protection officials inspect solar energy and lighting products at a shopping centre in Bangkok on May 20, 2026. (Photo: Somchai Poomlard)
Good start
The government’s energy transition measures, particularly its promotion of household rooftop solar installations, are a good starting point for a shift to cleaner energy, said Areeporn Asawinpongphan, an energy policy specialist at Thailand Development Research Institute (TDRI).
If Thailand can support greater electricity generation from solar power, it would reduce the need to import fuel from abroad, particularly liquefied natural gas (LNG).
“However, rooftop solar installations are most suitable for households that consume a significant amount of electricity during the daytime, and may not be suitable for every household,” she said.
“For households that use relatively little electricity during the day and consume more at night, installing rooftop solar without a battery storage system would provide them with very little benefit.”

items.title: Two Bangkok schools closed for 3 months over student brawls
items.summary: Two vocational colleges in central Bangkok have been ordered closed for three months as repeated brawls between their students have affected public safety and the economy, according to the higher education minister.
items.body_text:
Two vocational colleges in central Bangkok have been ordered closed for three months as repeated brawls between their students have affected public safety and the economy, according to the higher education minister.
Yodchanan Wongsawat issued the order on Wednesday after meeting with police and representatives of the two schools: Pathumwan Institute of Technology and Rajamangala University of Technology Tawan-ok, Uthenthawai Campus.
“This measure is aimed at restoring confidence to the Siam and Pathumwan areas which are vital to the economy, tourism and education,” Mr Yodchanan said.
The latest brawl happened at the elevated Siam BTS station on Monday morning when two students were stabbed.
It was reported that dozens of students from each school clashed with each other as nervous commuters looked on, while fewer than 10 police officers were on duty.
Uthenthawai had just resumed on-site education on Monday after being online since Aug 29. Students from both institutions also brawled on Aug 28 and 29.
The Siam station stands at the Pathumwan intersection, roughly halfway between the two campuses, which are only about 800 metres apart. The busiest station on the BTS network, it is a major interchange for commuters and tourists in inner Bangkok. (Story continues below)
“The problem concerns not only two institutions but also national security, image and confidence,” Mr Yodchanan said. “Pathumwan and Siam are economic, tourism and educational zones. Young people share those areas. So, safety is the priority.”
The suspension of on-site learning at both institutions took immediate effect. Mr Yodchanan said school officials concerned would organise alternative teaching programmes, while looking into speeding up the relocation of both institutions to end the feuds for good.
If solutions are not in place within the three-month period, the closure can be extended, the minister said.
Police would continue to stand guard in the vicinity of both institutions and would strictly enforce the law, he added.
Pol Lt Gen Siam Boonsom, commissioner of the Metropolitan Police Bureau, said leaders of both educational institutions agreed with the temporary suspension and would work out a plan to stop the rivalry.
Clashes between rival vocational college students in Thailand are as old as the schools themselves, but the Pathumwan-Uthenthawai rivalry is particularly notorious. Some brawls have led to fatalities and serious injuries, leading to temporary suspension of classes.
Uthenthawai, which began life in 1956 as Uthenthawai Builders School, sits on land leased from Chulalongkorn University, which has been trying to take back the land since 1975.
The Supreme Administrative Court in late 2023 ordered the school to move but protests from students and alumni have prevented the relocation from going ahead.

items.title: Policeman shoots teacher wife dead at kindergarten
items.summary: CHON BURI: A policeman shot his teacher wife to death while she was at work at a kindergarten in Bang Lamung district on Wednesday.
items.body_text:
CHON BURI: A policeman shot his teacher wife to death while she was at work at a kindergarten in Bang Lamung district on Wednesday.
The killing happened at Nong Pla Lai municipal school in tambon Nong Pla Lai at 10.30am. Police rushed to the school, found 44 frightened kindergarteners and six teachers and staff and evacuated them.
The body of the 48-year-old victim, identified as Pailin Thongthat, lay in the passage of the school canteen. She had been shot in the back of her neck.
Eyewitness Somyot Sanguanworapong, 57, said he saw a man arriving on a car. He approached the teacher and talked to her. The witness said he then heard a gunshot. Others ran away in fear while the gunman returned to his car and drove away.
Teachers kept their students in their classrooms for about 20 minutes, fearing that the gunman might remain in the school.
Pol Capt Manote Tipwet, deputy investigations inspector at Bang Lamung station, identified the gunman as Pol Sub Lt Tasapong Thongthat who was a patrol policeman at the same station.
After the shooting, the gunman returned to his house which is about three kilometres from the school and hid there.
Armed officers from the Bang Lamung police station, led by station chief Pol Col Sarawoot Nuchanat, surrounded the house in Flower Park Villa 2 housing estate and were attempting to persuade Pol Sub Lt Tasapong to surrender.
The motive for the shooting was not yet known. The school was closed for the remainder of the day. (Story continues below)
Security video shows the gunman walking towards his wife at the kindergarten at 10.38am on Wednesday. (Supplied photo)
Wednesday’s incident was the third shooting to take place at a school in Thailand in just over a month.
A rampage on Aug 7 at Debsirin Nonthaburi School left seven people dead, including the 14-year-old gunman, who had shot his grandparents to death earlier.
On Sept 2, a 14-year-old boy, the son of a policeman, was detained after he entered a secondary school in Kamphaeng Phet and fired off several shots. A security guard was grazed by one of the bullets.
Policemen with protective gear gather near the gunman’s house after the fatal shooting of his wife. (Photo: Amporn Sangkaew)

items.title: Indonesia airports reopen after Anak Krakatau ash, but Ili Lewotolok plume extends travel disruption
items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 9 — Volcanic ash from three more Indonesian volcanoes was reported across parts of the archipelago o...
items.body_text:
JAKARTA, Sept 9 — Volcanic ash from three more Indonesian volcanoes was reported across parts of the archipelago on Wednesday, in addition to Mount Anak Krakatau, with ash from one of them continuing to disrupt air travel in East Nusa Tenggara.
The Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) said analysis of Himawari-9 satellite imagery at 7am detected volcanic ash from Mount Ili Lewotolok in East Nusa Tenggara and Mount Dukono and Mount Ibu in North Maluku, alongside ash from Anak Krakatau in the Sunda Strait.
Of the four volcanoes, BMKG said ash from Ili Lewotolok, located on Lembata Island in East Nusa Tenggara in eastern Indonesia, was observed at the highest altitude of up to 8,000 feet (about 2,438 metres), moving northwest to north across parts of Lembata Regency and the Flores Strait.
“The public is urged not to panic, but to remain vigilant, continue monitoring information on volcanic ash distribution and refer to verified information from official sources,” the agency said in its latest post on social media.
Volcanic ash from Ili Lewotolok forced Wunopito Airport in Lewoleba to temporarily close on Tuesday, with the closure subsequently extended until an estimated 7am local time on Thursday, according to state-owned air navigation service provider AirNav Indonesia.
Meanwhile, all eight airports that have been temporarily closed since Sunday due to volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau had reopened by Tuesday, including Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, Indonesia’s main international gateway.
Separately, Lampung’s Regional Disaster Management Agency (BPBD) said a monitoring operation at 10am by the Indonesian Navy vessel KRI Lepu-861 found that eruptive activity at Anak Krakatau remained observable, marked by smoke and volcanic ash.
The agency said the monitoring, which also drew on Himawari-9 satellite imagery, detected ash reaching up to 7,000 feet (about 2,134 metres) and moving northwest, covering part of Lampung Bay. — Bernama

items.title: FlightRadar24 reports 177 cancellations, cyberattack ruled out as UK travellers suffer ongoing chaos
items.summary: LONDON, Sept 9 — UK air travellers faced more misery Wednesday with 177 flights scrapped across the country, as Br...
items.body_text:
LONDON, Sept 9 — UK air travellers faced more misery Wednesday with 177 flights scrapped across the country, as Britain’s air traffic control service scrambled to recover from a technical glitch which it ruled out as a cyberattack.
Aircraft tracking website FlightRadar24 revealed the fresh cancellations after 1,300 flights to and from UK airports were axed Tuesday, with tens of thousands of customers affected at British Airways alone.
Nearly all the latest flights were at London Heathrow, Britain’s busiest airport, FlightRadar24 wrote on X.
The head of the National Air Traffic Services (NATS), Martin Rolfe, meanwhile said “we have at this point ruled out cyber” as a cause.
“We don’t believe it was a cyberattack,” he told BBC Radio.
Rolfe said NATS will be doing a “very, very thorough” investigation into what exactly caused the incident.
NATS warned in an X post late Tuesday that “it will take time to recover” from the outage.
UK news outlets reported that British Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander had summoned Rolfe to a meeting with her on Wednesday.
Rolfe earlier told Sky News that he accepted “full responsibility” but declined to say if he was considering quitting his job.
Alexander said on X that she was “seeking assurances that lessons will be learned and systems that support aviation are up to the job”.
Neal McMahon, chief operations officer at Irish no-frills airline Ryanair, called for Rolfe to be fired, accusing him of having “failed UK travellers”.
‘Knock-on impact’
Heathrow said late Tuesday that departures had resumed, after the “technical issue” forced the airport to suspend arrivals.
But it warned that “disruption is expected to continue”, asking passengers in an X post to check with their airline before travelling to the airport.
The air traffic chaos follow a technical glitch in July last year that saw scores of flights to and from the UK cancelled, prompting anger from airline chiefs.
Britain meanwhile suffered its worst air systems failure in years in 2023, with more than 700,000 passengers affected after hundreds of flights were delayed or cancelled.
Responding to the latest fallout, NATS said: “We know this is hugely frustrating and apologise unreservedly.”
‘Absolute nightmare’
Caught up by the glitch, healthcare worker Josie Donoghue said it had been “an absolute nightmare” at London’s Gatwick airport, having had to disembark her flight to Ireland after three hours stuck on the runway.
“Getting through that airport was like trying to get out of Alcatraz,” she told Britain’s domestic Press Association news agency.
Liverpool, Birmingham and Edinburgh airports were also affected, while Dublin airport said it had cancelled dozens of flights.
Ryanair said more than 65,000 of its passengers had been disrupted and it had cancelled more than 50 flights.
English football club Arsenal, due to play Napoli in the Champions League Wednesday in the southern Italian city, was forced to cancel a news conference after the team’s flight was delayed. — AFP

items.title: Washington slams Chinese AI firms for ‘systematic’ theft of US model capabilities
items.summary: WASHINGTON, Sept 9 — Washington accused top Chinese artificial intelligence labs including DeepSeek and Moonshot A...
items.body_text:
WASHINGTON, Sept 9 — Washington accused top Chinese artificial intelligence labs including DeepSeek and Moonshot AI of systematically stealing the capabilities of American models today as the two countries race for tech supremacy.
The advisory from the US cyber defence agency comes ahead of an expected meeting this month between President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping at the White House, where AI could be an important discussion topic.
It follows several previous accusations of Chinese AI theft through a process known as distillation, levelled by the US government and American AI companies.
“China-based artificial intelligence (AI) companies are conducting systematic extraction of proprietary functionalities and capabilities of US AI companies’ models,” yesterday’s advisory read.
They are doing so “through industrial-scale knowledge distillation campaigns that form the core — not merely a supplement — of their AI development strategy”, it said.
Distillation is where an AI model is trained to mimic the output of a larger, more capable one.
The method is widely used across the industry, but Washington says Chinese firms have deployed it at scale to illicitly copy American systems.
Chinese companies that adopt this strategy “see significantly shorter AI development timelines and reduced financial expenditures in training a frontier model”, the advisory said.
It detailed how DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, MiniMax, StepFun, and Z.AI allegedly used millions of exchanges and requests to steal the capabilities of US models from the likes of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and xAI.
These actions, taken “likely with Chinese government awareness”, have taken place since at least late 2024, it said.
AFP contacted the Chinese companies apart from StepFun which was not immediately reachable. Moonshot AI declined to comment.
Trump is under pressure to respond to the increasing success of Chinese AI models that many companies prefer to the more powerful, but pricier, US versions from Anthropic or OpenAI.
In July, dozens of startups wrote a letter to the Trump administration urging it to think twice against any outright ban or strict curbs on foreign-made AI models, saying this should only be considered for government use of the technology.
That month, Beijing also turned the tables by accusing US AI of using Chinese examples to train their models.
Asked about the accusations at a regular briefing today, Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said she had not seen the specific US report but the country should “refrain from making unfounded accusations against and smearing China”.
“The development of artificial intelligence in China is the result of achieving high-level self-reliance and strength in science and technology,” she said.
“Both China and the United States are major countries in the field of AI. We should strengthen cooperation.” — AFP

items.title: Amazon set to raise over $5 billion in first sterling bond sale, lead managers say
items.body_text:
Amazon set to raise over $5 billion in first sterling bond sale, lead managers say
LONDON, Sept 9 : Amazon was set to raise 4 billion pounds ($5.43 billion) from its first ever sterling bond sale on Wednesday that drew strong demand, according to a bank managing the deal, as hyperscalers rush to diversify their funding sources to finance the AI boom.
The deal is the latest example of how hyperscalers are increasingly selling bonds across markets outside of the U.S. this year, from euros to Swiss francs and the yen, as they make sure they can raise capital wherever they can, given their huge funding needs.
They have already issued more than $200 billion of debt this year, more than doubling from the whole of 2025, according to LSEG data.
Amazon saw over 12 billion pounds in demand for the four-part deal, which will is expected to raise 1 billion pounds each from 3-, 6-, 12- and 19-year bonds, according to the memo sent by the lead manager seen by Reuters.
They will price to offer spreads of 53 basis points, 75 basis points, 90 basis points and 93 basis points over corresponding British government bonds, the memo added.
The pound is the latest currency Amazon has added to its funding programme after tapping the euro, Swiss franc and Canadian dollar bond markets.
The European Central Bank warned earlier in September that hyperscalers' push into the euro zone bond market could potentially crowd out other borrowers and push up their financing costs.
Google-parent Alphabet, was the first hyperscaler to tap the sterling market in February, when it raised £5.5 billion from a five-part deal, including a rare 100-year bond. It has also raised Japanese yen, Canadian and Australian dollar debt this year.
According to LSEG data, this is Amazon's first bond sale since July, when it received weaker demand than in the past for a $25-billion offering, in one of several signs that the heavy pace of hyperscaler borrowing has started to test the limits of investor demand.
($1 = 0.7373 pounds)

items.title: No current plans to designate Tagore forest as a nature reserve: Chee Hong Tat
items.summary: The forest located near Upper Thomson Road is zoned for residential use.
items.body_text:
No current plans to designate Tagore forest as a nature reserve: Chee Hong Tat
The forest located near Upper Thomson Road is zoned for residential use.
SINGAPORE: The government currently has no plans to designate Tagore forest as a nature reserve, Minister for National Development Chee Hong Tat said on Tuesday (Sep 8).
Mr Chee was responding to questions from Members of Parliament (MPs) on land planning assessment and decision-making for ecologically significant sites.
MP Kenneth Tiong (WP-Aljunied) asked about nature reserves gazetted under the Parks and Trees Act, and whether the government will consider designating Tagore forest as a nature reserve.
The forest, located southeast of the intersection between Seletar Expressway and Upper Thomson Road, is currently zoned for residential use under the Urban Redevelopment Authority’s (URA) masterplan.
In 2024, over 40 scientists and conservationists proposed studying the protection of the forest as a nature park in a document called the Singapore Terrestrial Conservation Plan. The forest represents a buffer zone surrounding the Central Catchment Nature Reserve that is a refuge for rare wildlife such as the Raffles' banded langur.
Mr Chee said in his written parliamentary answer that the government adopts a “science-based” approach to prioritising what and how they conserve.
In deciding to designate an area as a nature reserve, the government considers its biodiversity and ecological value, and its importance to Singapore’s native biodiversity.
These considerations are weighed alongside Singapore’s other land-use needs, he said.
Singapore has four nature reserves protected and conserved under the Park and Trees Act. Bukit Timah Nature Reserve and Central Catchment Nature Reserve were gazetted in 1990, while Labrador Nature Reserve and Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve were gazetted in 2002.
“These are assessed to be the most biodiverse areas in Singapore and are representative of Singapore’s native landscapes. They also safeguard a range of habitats and serve as strongholds for various endemic and threatened species,” Mr Chee said.
Mr Chee said URA works closely with the National Parks Board (NParks) to consider ecology and biodiversity in the Long-Term Plan and Master Plan, and integrates development and conservation upstream in their land use planning processes.
He noted that more than 7,800ha of green spaces have been set aside in Singapore, which would increase to 8,800ha by 2035.
The minister said the government has designated nature areas and nature parks as buffers to nature reserves, and set aside parks and other green spaces that serve both ecological and recreational functions.
NParks’ island-wide Ecological Profiling Exercise helps agencies identify key ecological corridors that support connectivity between core habitats, and locate critical wildlife corridors that require monitoring, such as EcoLink@BKE, he said.
"This enables us to integrate nature into our urban environment and everyday lives," he added.
MEETING HOUSING SUPPLY
On planning new housing supply, Mr Chee said the agencies take into account demographic and socioeconomic trends, prevailing market conditions, and the supply of resale flats on the open market to meet Singaporeans’ needs across different locations and time periods.
This includes providing housing near existing estates as many Singaporeans, including young families, seniors and singles, want to continue living near their families for mutual care and support, he said.
“It is not possible to predict future housing demand with 100 per cent accuracy as the key demand drivers have varying degrees of uncertainty. Nevertheless, we expect housing demand to remain strong in the near to medium term, due to strong household formation rates and decreasing household sizes,” he said.

items.title: Raikkonen's son Robin joins Red Bull's driver development programme
items.body_text:
Raikkonen's son Robin joins Red Bull's driver development programme
Sept 9 : Robin Raikkonen, the 11-year-old son of 2007 world champion Kimi Raikkonen, has become the latest prospect to join Red Bull's driver development programme, the Formula One team announced on Wednesday.
Nicknamed 'Ace', Robin has shown promise in karting championships and will start working with the team from 2027 in a programme that has produced F1 drivers such as Sebastian Vettel and Max Verstappen - both four-times champions.
"We are all thrilled and excited that Robin has been chosen to further his racing path as a member of the Red Bull Junior Team," Kimi said in a statement.
"They offer a compelling and comprehensive programme to develop and nurture Robin's progress over the coming years and provide him with all the experience required to develop his natural talent, which has amply been displayed in all his karting endeavours to date."
The famously laconic Raikkonen raced in over 350 Formula One Grands Prix, claiming 21 wins and 103 podiums. He has also participated in the World Rally Championship and tried his hand at NASCAR.
The Finn, nicknamed 'Iceman', was the last Ferrari driver to win the F1 championship, claiming his sole title in 2007.
Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies said Robin had "already demonstrated exceptional ability in karting" while praising his speed and racecraft.
"Our goal is to develop him step by step, without placing any unnecessary pressure on his shoulders," Mekies said.
"The path through motorsport is a long one, and we will give him the time, support and resources he needs to maximise his potential."
Robin follows in the footsteps of Ella Hakkinen, the daughter of Finland's double world champion Mika, who joined McLaren's driver development programme last year.

items.title: Costa Rican man, 119, seeks recognition as world's oldest person
items.summary: SARDINAL, Costa Rica, Sept 9 - In a modest wooden home in Sardinal, about a 20-minute drive from Costa Rica's Pacific coast, Jose Flores spends his days napping, eating meals prepared by his granddaughter, and arm-wrestling with her.
items.body_text:
Costa Rican man, 119, seeks recognition as world's oldest person
SARDINAL, Costa Rica, Sept 9 - In a modest wooden home in Sardinal, about a 20-minute drive from Costa Rica's Pacific coast, Jose Flores spends his days napping, eating meals prepared by his granddaughter, and arm-wrestling with her.
His family and official records indicate that he is 119 years old, which would make him the world's oldest man, though international verification of his birth date is still pending as specialists review historical documents.
Sardinal is a hot town on the Nicoya Peninsula, one of the world's five regions commonly known as Blue Zones, where people tend to live longer and healthier lives and are more likely to reach the age of 100.
Residents attribute their longevity to calcium- and magnesium-rich water, a diet based on corn and beans, physical work, and strong family and community ties.
Hellen Flores, Jose's granddaughter and carer, said her grandfather, who spent his life working in the countryside, now lives "calmly and happily." From time to time, he recalls stories from his life, tells the occasional joke and says one of the secrets to his long life is his family.
"Without love, without affection, without care, he would not still be here," she said.
For Jorge Vindas, founder of the Nicoya Peninsula Blue Zone Association, which studies longevity in the region, other factors also help explain longevity cases such as Flores'.
According to his identity card, Flores was born on July 11, 1907.
"Family and social networks are number one, along with spirituality and the strong faith of these people, who are very physically active," Vindas said. He added that they eat healthily and lead calm, low-stress lives.
On the verification process, Vindas said the association has historical records that still need to be confirmed by international organizations, including Guinness World Records.
"We have a large number of documents, from the birth certificate and baptism certificate to documents from later in life, when he was already a father and beyond," he said. "Once all that documentation is reviewed, we hope it will be validated and that we will have good news soon."
As the validation process continues, Flores' family is awaiting an answer that Hellen Flores said would carry meaning beyond their own household.
"It would be a source of pride, both for the family and for the country," she said.
Flores had eight children and now has 23 grandchildren, 25 great-grandchildren and one great-great-granddaughter.
The world's oldest living person is Ethel Caterham of Britain. Born on August 21, 1909, in Hampshire, England, she turned 117 in 2026. She was recognized as the world's oldest living person after Brazilian nun Inah Canabarro Lucas died in April 2025. REUTERS

items.title: Russia says it hopes US-mediated talks with Ukraine will resume soon
items.summary: MOSCOW, Sept 9 - Russia hopes that U.S.-mediated peace talks on ending the war in Ukraine will resume soon, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Wednesday.
items.body_text:
Russia says it hopes US-mediated talks with Ukraine will resume soon
MOSCOW, Sept 9 - Russia hopes that U.S.-mediated peace talks on ending the war in Ukraine will resume soon, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Wednesday.
No such talks between Russia and Ukraine have taken place since February, but President Donald Trump sent his negotiators to Moscow and then Kyiv at the weekend in a bid to relaunch the stalled process.
Peskov was responding to a comment by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio that it may be possible to draw up a roadmap to restart talks and work towards an acceptable outcome for both sides.
A huge gulf remains between Russia and Ukraine on how to end the 4-1/2-year war, with Kyiv rejecting Moscow's demands that it give up more territory.
Peskov said Moscow would not publicly discuss any specifics of a potential settlement, but there was a "confirmed political will" to resume talks.
"We hope that these negotiations will resume in the foreseeable future, and we remain in contact with our American counterparts," he said, a day after Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke by phone.
Peskov added that the issue of exchanging prisoners between Russia and the U.S. was "a constant item on the agenda", including between the two presidents. He noted that Russia had released one American prisoner, Robert Gilman, at Trump's request last month.
The two countries have traded prisoners at several points in the past few years.
The biggest such deal was in August 2024, when Russia got back eight prisoners held in the West, including a member of its FSB security service convicted of murder in Germany.
In exchange, 16 people were released from Russian and Belarusian jails. Among those freed by Moscow were prominent Russian dissidents and three U.S. citizens, including Wall Street Journal correspondent Evan Gershkovich. REUTERS

items.title: ‘They’re playing with our lives’: AI researcher quits Anthropic
items.summary: AI could wipe out humanity by the end of the decade at the rate things are going, he warns.
items.body_text:
‘They’re playing with our lives’: AI researcher quits Anthropic
- AI researcher Jacob Coxon quit Anthropic, accusing AI firms of recklessly rushing to build self-improving superintelligent models that could threaten human survival.
- Anthropic acknowledges AI risks, admits that it lacks a clear plan to control superintelligent AI.
- Industry leaders urge coordinated AI development slowdowns and regulation, with recent legislative efforts aiming to suspend AI progress until federal oversight is established.
AI generated
SAN FRANCISCO – An artificial intelligence researcher who left OpenAI to join Anthropic has decided to leave the industry, accusing both US companies of “playing with our lives” in the race to develop AI models capable of self-improvement.
Jacob Coxon, 27, spent the past three years pretraining AI models, first at OpenAI and then, in 2026, at its rival Anthropic, which he considered more cautious in its approach.
Pretraining is the stage where AI models absorb vast quantities of data.
“Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives,” Coxon said on Sept 8.
“The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” he said in a post on X.
“This is not a marketing stunt,” he added.
Superintelligence is the theoretical point when AI’s capabilities exceed human intelligence.
Anthropic safety executive Evan Hubinger backed up Coxon on X.
“We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans!” he said, adding that he estimated that risk at more than 10 per cent over the next decade.
Hubinger said Anthropic is “trying its best”, but does not yet have a plan to ensure an AI system that surpasses human capabilities would obey its creators. He said there was a “low” risk of that happening with current models.
Coxon’s resignation comes as Anthropic prepares for its market debut, following a summer marked by unauthorised hacks carried out by AI tools during testing.
AI leaders say so-called recursive self-improvement, a stage where AI systems could essentially design and train the next generation of AI with little human involvement, is drawing near.
Coxon considers Anthropic’s efforts genuine but said he believes no company can responsibly develop an AI that surpasses humans without government intervention or a coordinated slowdown.
“At Anthropic, the stakes are well-understood, but they are locked in a race to get there first. They believe no one else will act responsibly, so they must do it themselves, despite the risk,” he said.
In February, Anthropic removed a pledge from its safety charter to halt the development of its models if it fails to control their risks.
It argued that if it unilaterally pauses its work, its less cautious rivals will dominate the industry, making it less safe overall.
At the end of July, more than 1,000 tech industry employees, including Anthropic’s chief executive Dario Amodei, called on Washington to support a coordinated slowdown in the development of the most advanced AI systems.
OpenAI halted training of its latest models for two weeks in August before resuming it under tighter controls.
On Sept 13, OpenAI’s chief scientist, Jakub Pachocki, called for “extreme caution”.
“International coordination on future AI development needs to become a top priority for governments around the world,” he said in a blog post.
AI models are not regulated by federal law in the United States.
In September, Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Greg Casar introduced a Bill seeking to suspend AI development until a federal regulator is created. AFP

items.title: Election interference activities revealed
items.body_text:
- 
            Election interference activities revealedBALLOT INTEGRITY: Groups engaging in activities such as unlicensed money lending and election betting often serve Beijing’s vote disruption efforts, authorities said
  - By Lu Yun-feng, Jonathan Chin and Sam Garcia / Staff reporter, with staff writers and CNA
 The authorities have launched 54 probes into suspected foreign election interference and other electoral fraud-related crimes to protect the integrity of the Nov. 28 local elections, the Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau said yesterday. Special agents launched investigations into illegal foreign campaign contributions, money laundering and election betting ahead of the “nine-in-one” elections, the bureau said. The investigations resulted in 25 pretrial detentions, 70 suspects placed on bail, and the confiscation of NT$62.8 billion (US$2 billion) linked to suspected illegal cash flows used in breaking election laws, it said. Huang Wen-yang, head of the Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau’s Criminal Investigation Division, speaks at a press conference in New Taipei City yesterday, saying authorities had uncovered 54 cases involving more than NT$62.8 billion in illicit funds.Photo: CNA The bureau interviewed 559 people as potential suspects or witnesses, it added. The investigations were part of the law enforcement effort to prevent foreign election interference, it said, adding that it is focusing on unlicensed money lending, election betting, and money launderers operating under shell corporations and virtual buyer groups. Organizations and groups engaging in such activities often serve as conduits for funds used in election interference by Beijing, it said. Another goal of the operation is to identify those who benefited from the Chinese government’s illegal campaign contributions, it said. The bureau said it assigned 25 field offices to the effort, seizing NT$11.19 billion from unregistered moneylenders, NT$4.24 billion from alleged launderers and N$5.06 billion from alleged tax evaders. The seizures included NT$153 million in cash, 521 bank accounts holding a total of NT$501 million, Tether cryptocurrency valued at US$2,184, 12 luxury cars valued at NT$23 million, luxury fashion accessories valued at NT$9.1 million, watches valued at NT$10 million and 35 properties valued at NT$101 million, the bureau said. The properties and assets were deemed proceeds from suspected criminal activities, it said. The bureau warned political candidates and members of the public against receiving or facilitating the transfer of suspicious funds from China or other countries. Protecting elections’ integrity is a national security matter, and money laundering prevention is necessary to ensure the orderly functioning of the financial market, it added. Separately yesterday, the High Prosecutors’ Office said that prosecutors uncovered 212 cases of illicit financial transactions intended to influence the elections, seizing more than NT$900 million in suspected criminal proceeds. The office launched a crackdown on illicit financial flows nationwide from Aug. 17 to Friday last week to prevent illicit funds from influencing the elections, prosecutors said in a news release. The operation uncovered 212 cases involving illicit financial flows and 588 people suspected of breaching the Banking Act (銀行法), the Money Laundering Control Act (洗錢防制法) and gambling provisions of the Criminal Code, they said. Prosecutors detained 75 people, while 229 were released on bail, and the remainder were subject to other measures, including residence restrictions, it added. Authorities seized about NT$909 million in suspected criminal proceeds in cash and bank accounts, as well as more than 390,000 Tether tokens, 20 vehicles and 850 electronic devices, such as mobile phones, tablets and computers, the office said. They also seized 36 properties and more than 100 luxury items, including designer bags, watches and gold jewelry, it added.

items.title: Japan delegations urge closer Taiwan cooperation
items.body_text:
- 
            Japan delegations urge closer Taiwan cooperation
  - Staff writer, with CNA
 A senior member of the Japan Innovation Party (JIP) yesterday called for closer Tokyo-Taipei cooperation, including on drone and space-based technologies, to meet modern defense needs and promote regional peace and stability. Nobuyuki Baba, former JIP leader and head of the party’s Japan-Republic of China Friendship Study Group, met earlier yesterday with President William Lai (賴清德) at the Presidential Office in Taipei, and discussed bilateral relations, US-China ties and other issues. Speaking at a press briefing, Baba thanked Taiwan for its generous donations to help people affected by a magnitude 7.1 earthquake that struck Japan’s Kumamoto Prefecture late last month, causing widespread infrastructure damage and transportation disruptions and killing at least 38 people. Nobuyuki Baba, left, head of the Japan Innovation Party’s Japan-Republic of China Friendship Study Group, clinks mugs with President William Lai at the Presidential Office in Taipei yesterday.Photo: Screen grab from the Presidential Office’s Flickr page “True friendship reveals itself through adversity,” he said, adding that Japan and Taiwan have always been there for each other in times of crisis. The Taiwanese government said that a dedicated bank account set up to accept private donations for the quake had reached more than NT$300 million (US$9.51 million). The government also donated NT$5 million to support reconstruction efforts in Kumamoto, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said. Baba said his delegation and Lai agreed that both sides should continue to deepen bilateral cooperation and exchanges in areas such as the economy, culture, tourism and natural disaster preparedness. On regional security, Baba said that Lai told him that Taiwan is strengthening its self-defense capabilities. The Japanese government is also considering strengthening its self-defense capabilities amid rising regional and global tensions, he said. The JIP, the junior coalition partner of Japan’s ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), also hopes to harness drone and space-based technologies to revolutionize national defense and logistics and meet the challenges posed by modern warfare, Baba said. Tokyo and Taipei should work together to complement each other’s capabilities and jointly develop cutting-edge technologies, including drones, he said. At the meeting, Lai told the JIP delegation that Taiwan looks forward to an even stronger partnership between the two countries under the LDP-JIP coalition, to jointly build a “non-red” supply chain, thereby enhancing the resilience of global democratic supply chains and strengthening economic and trade cooperation, Lai said. Separately yesterday, a delegation from the Japanese cross-party parliamentary group “Diet Members’ Association for Peace and Stability in the Taiwan Strait” arrived in Taipei for a three-day visit. The delegation is led by Haruo Kitamura, a member of the House of Councilors from the Conservative Party of Japan. Kitamura said Taiwan is Japan’s most important friend, adding that peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait are important not only to Taiwan, but also “vital to Japan’s very survival.” He specifically cited two legislative goals, pointing to the US’ Taiwan Relations Act and Taiwan Travel Act. He said Japan must, “by all means,” pass its own versions of the two laws to allow Japan to work with the US to continue conveying to the world the close ties between Japan and Taiwan and their peoples. “Only by doing so can we take the most critical step toward safeguarding peace and stability in the Taiwan Strait,” he said. Additional reporting by Fang Wei-li

items.title: Medical visits top 110,000 as flu epidemic spreads
items.body_text:
- 
            Medical visits top 110,000 as flu epidemic spreads
  - By Lee I-chia / Staff reporter
 The seasonal flu has entered an epidemic period, with more than 110,000 medical visits, 19 deaths and 105 severe cases reported last week, the Centers for Disease Control (CDC) said yesterday. The centers also reported the youngest severe COVID-19 case on record in Taiwan and two new cases of acute hepatitis C linked to a cluster in New Taipei City. Influenza and COVID-19 viruses were the most common respiratory pathogen spreading locally in the past four weeks, CDC Epidemic Intelligence Center Director Guo Hung-wei (郭宏偉) said, adding that influenza A(H1N1) was the dominant flu strain detected. Centers for Disease Control Epidemic Intelligence Center Director Guo Hung-wei speaks at a news conference in Taipei yesterday.Photo: CNA There were 115,136 medical visits for flu-like illnesses from Aug. 30 to Saturday last week, 11.2 percent of which were emergency cases, surpassing the epidemic threshold of 11 percent, he said. “We have entered the flu epidemic period,” he said. A total of 105 severe flu cases and 19 flu-related deaths were confirmed between Tuesday last week and Monday, and more than 80 percent of them have or had chronic underlying conditions, he said. As for COVID-19, there were 20,199 medical visits from Aug. 30 to Saturday last week, slightly lower than the week before, but still at a relatively high level, he said, adding that 73 severe cases and 15 deaths were confirmed between Tuesday last week and Monday. Among the severe COVID-19 cases was a less than month-old baby who does not have underlying health conditions, and is not eligible for vaccination, making it the youngest severe case on record, CDC physician Lin Yung-ching (林詠青) said. The boy had a mild fever and nose congestion late last month and was taken to see a doctor the next day, but as his symptoms persisted, he was hospitalized this month and later transferred to an intensive care unit when he experienced difficulty breathing and respiratory distress, and was confirmed to have pneumonia, he said. Contact tracing found that the boy had been exposed to a person who has COVID-19, Lin added. CDC Deputy Director-General Lin Min-cheng (林明誠) said that medical visits for flu-like illness last week was the highest of the same week in a decade, and is expected to continue increasing in the next four weeks. While COVID-19 cases have dropped, severe cases and the number of deaths remain high, he added. The CDC also provided an update on a cluster of confirmed acute viral hepatitis C cases traced to a clinic in New Taipei City, with two more cases identified through expanded testing, Lin Min-cheng said. The CDC last week reported 11 confirmed cases who all received injections at the Antai Songhe Clinic (安泰淞鶴診所). With the onset of symptoms occurring between Jan. 29 and Aug. 18, 1,118 people who received an injection at the clinic between July 1 last year and Aug. 27 are urged to get a blood test, it said. As of Monday, 1,096 people have been notified and 353 have ben tested, Lin Min-cheng said. Two were confirmed to have acute viral hepatitis C — a woman in her 60s who is asymptomatic and a man in his 50s who has symptoms including loss of appetite, dark urine and general fatigue, and has been hospitalized for treatment, he said. Experts had estimated that the positivity rate would be about 5 percent, but so far only two had been confirmed among the 353 tested, which is an encouraging sign, he said, adding that testing and follow-ups were ongoing. Symptoms of acute viral hepatitis C may vary, so the absence of symptoms does not necessarily mean no infection, he said, urging those who have been notified to get tested as soon as possible.

items.title: Buildings Dep’t launches 259 prosecutions over works at fire-hit Wang Fuk Court, 9 months after fatal blaze
items.summary: Hong Kong’s Buildings Department (BD) has launched more than 200 prosecutions against four individuals and two companies that were responsible for overseeing renovation works at fire-hit Wang Fuk Court when a deadly blaze tore through the estate last year. The 259 charges, covering the use of defective or substandard materials and failure to adequately supervise […]
items.body_text:
Hong Kong’s Buildings Department (BD) has launched more than 200 prosecutions against four individuals and two companies that oversaw renovation works at the fire-hit Wang Fuk Court.
The 259 charges, covering the use of defective or substandard materials and failure to adequately supervise renovation works, were initiated on Wednesday – more than nine months after the fire broke out.
The prosecutions were launched after a joint investigation by the BD and the Housing Bureau’s Independent Checking Unit (ICU), the Wednesday statement said.
The blaze at Wang Fuk Court, a government-subsidised housing estate in Tai Po, killed 168 people and displaced thousands of residents in November last year.
Nine months on
“The investigation revealed that the Registered Inspector (RI) employed by the project consultant failed to properly supervise the prescribed repair works and failed to ensure that the building was safe or had been rendered safe,” the department said on Wednesday
“Meanwhile, during the course of the works, the main contractor and the project consultant allegedly permitted or authorised the use of non-fire-retardant scaffold netting and tarpaulins, as well as non-fire-retardant styrofoam boards to cover windows,” it continued.
Fireproof windows along the emergency fire escape stairwell were also removed to create temporary access openings, causing smoke and fire to pour into the buildings and “ultimately resulting in 168 fatalities and 79 injuries,” the statement read.
The two prosecuted companies are Will Power Architects, consultants for the estate’s HK$330 million renovation project, and the main contractor, Prestige Construction & Engineering.
The four prosecuted individuals are Will Power’s director Wong Hap-yin and the inspector employed by the company, Wilson Ng, as well as Prestige’s two directors Hau Wa-kin and Ho Kin-yip.
The same four people were also charged with a slew of offences in June, with Wong, Ng, Ho, and the two companies they represent facing manslaughter charges.
‘Widespread systemic issues’
Similar findings have previously been detailed in evidentiary hearings set up by an independent committee to probe the cause of the fire and its rapid spread.
In March, the committee heard that the blaze revealed “widespread systemic issues” ranging from potential collusive tendering to rubber-stamp inspections and unauthorised proxy votes.
The companies and the four individuals were discussed extensively at the hearings, though they did not testify in person.
The BD and the Housing Bureau’s ICU have also been subject to scrutiny in the independent committee’s evidentiary hearings, with a senior government surveyor admitting to alerting the consultant ahead of site checks before the estate went up in flames.
The Wednesday statement said that the BD has stepped up regulation, site inspections, and enforcement actions since the Wang Fuk Court fire. This includes requiring fire-retardancy test reports, conducting random spot checks, and launching an inspection operation for 400 renovation projects citywide.

items.title: Washington accuses Chinese AI firms of ‘systematic’ theft
items.summary: Washington accused top Chinese artificial intelligence labs including DeepSeek and Moonshot AI of systematically stealing the capabilities of American models on Tuesday as the two countries race for tech supremacy. The advisory from the US cyber defense agency comes ahead of an expected meeting this month between President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi […]
items.body_text:
Washington accused top Chinese artificial intelligence labs including DeepSeek and Moonshot AI of systematically stealing the capabilities of American models on Tuesday as the two countries race for tech supremacy.
The advisory from the US cyber defense agency comes ahead of an expected meeting this month between President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping at the White House, where AI could be an important discussion topic.
It follows several previous accusations of Chinese AI theft through a process known as distillation, levelled by the US government and American AI companies.
“China-based artificial intelligence (AI) companies are conducting systematic extraction of proprietary functionalities and capabilities of US AI companies’ models,” Tuesday’s advisory read.
They are doing so “through industrial-scale knowledge distillation campaigns that form the core — not merely a supplement — of their AI development strategy”, it said.
Distillation is where an AI model is trained to mimic the output of a larger, more capable one.
The method is widely used across the industry, but Washington says Chinese firms have deployed it at scale to illicitly copy American systems.
Chinese companies that adopt this strategy “see significantly shorter AI development timelines and reduced financial expenditures in training a frontier model”, the advisory said.
It detailed how DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, MiniMax, StepFun, and Z.AI allegedly used millions of exchanges and requests to steal the capabilities of US models from the likes of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and xAI.
These actions, taken “likely with Chinese government awareness”, have taken place since at least late 2024, it said.
AFP contacted the Chinese companies apart from StepFun which was not immediately reachable. Moonshot AI declined to comment.
‘Smearing China’
Trump is under pressure to respond to the increasing success of Chinese AI models that many companies prefer to the more powerful, but pricier, US versions from Anthropic or OpenAI.
In July, dozens of startups wrote a letter to the Trump administration urging it to think twice against any outright ban or strict curbs on foreign-made AI models, saying this should only be considered for government use of the technology.
That month, Beijing also turned the tables by accusing US AI of using Chinese examples to train their models.
Asked about the accusations at a regular briefing Wednesday, Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said she had not seen the specific US report but the country should “refrain from making unfounded accusations against and smearing China”.
“The development of artificial intelligence in China is the result of achieving high-level self-reliance and strength in science and technology,” she said.
“Both China and the United States are major countries in the field of AI. We should strengthen cooperation.”

items.title: ‘Long live Chairman Mao’: Supporters pay respects to founder of Communist China
items.summary: Fifty years after his death, diehard fans of the Chinese Communist leader Mao Zedong lined up Wednesday in his hometown to pay homage, holding portraits, flags and huge floral tributes. Chairman Mao, the founder of the People’s Republic, died on September 9, 1976, and his life and legacy was being commemorated fervently this week by […]
items.body_text:
Fifty years after his death, diehard fans of the Chinese Communist leader Mao Zedong lined up Wednesday in his hometown to pay homage, holding portraits, flags and huge floral tributes.
Chairman Mao, the founder of the People’s Republic, died on September 9, 1976, and his life and legacy was being commemorated fervently this week by those who still revere him as a visionary leader.
As China grapples with a slowing economy, nostalgia is growing for Mao’s egalitarian ideals, but his drastic policies are also blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths.
Tourists — many of them university students — laid chrysanthemum wreaths, bottles of Chinese alcohol, and cigarettes at the foot of a 10-metre-tall bronze statue of Mao in the main square in Shaoshan, in central Hunan province.
Hundreds of visitors lined up in carefully organised queues to bow solemnly and observe a few seconds of silence, while others posed for photos in front of the statue.
Watchful police stopped people from lingering too long.
Deng, a 28-year-old tourist, told AFP that he had “been influenced” by Mao’s spirit and had great respect for him.
“I suddenly felt like coming here today to commemorate him, because the 50th anniversary is something that only comes around once in a lifetime.”
The night before, around 1,000 ardent admirers — some in the short, tunic-style suits famously worn by Mao — held an emotional ceremony at the statue.
They brandished relics of a bygone era: old portraits of the leader and copies of the “Little Red Book”, a collection of his quotations that was once virtually ubiquitous in China.
“Long live Chairman Mao!” the group roared repeatedly, some pumping their fists in the air and singing revolutionary songs.
Reminders of Mao are peppered all around the otherwise nondescript village of Shaoshan, propelled to fame by the man who would become known as the “Great Helmsman”.
‘Never forget’
Busloads of visitors were arriving at Mao’s remote hometown, where he was born in December 1893.
Shaoshan has been promoted by state media as a spot for “red tourism” — part of Beijing’s decades-long push to bring tourists enamoured by the country’s communist history to key landmarks.
Visitors formed a snaking queue to enter Mao’s childhood home, which overlooked rice paddies that a sign claimed he helped to cultivate when he was young.
“We must never forget the people who dug the well from which we drink,” 63-year-old Jing Shiming told AFP, visiting from Shanghai.
Mao and leaders from his generation “transformed China from a backward and impoverished… country into the prosperous and strong nation it is today”, he said.
Although his legacy has at times proved difficult for the country’s central leadership, Mao is still emblematic of the Chinese Communist Party.
His face is emblazoned on banknotes; many Chinese taxi drivers hang good luck charms bearing his face from their rear-view mirrors; and a large portrait of him takes pride of place overlooking Tiananmen Square in Beijing.
Souvenir stores in Shaoshan sold hordes of Mao paraphernalia including badges, bronze figurines, caps and T-shirts.
Shop owner Ouyang Qianli said she was overjoyed to see people from all around China descend on the village to pay their respects to “Grandpa Mao”.
“He was selfless and pioneered a new era for China,” the 40-year-old added.
Memories fading
Mao’s time in power, however, was marked by tens of millions of deaths from famine during the Great Leap Forward, and the bloody Cultural Revolution he engineered.
Widely seen as China’s most shameful and destructive period since the Communist Party swept to power, the latter campaign pushed the country to the brink of economic and social collapse.
But while the party acknowledged those decades as a “mistake”, Mao is still painted as a hero in the official narrative, with state media hailing him as “a great proletarian revolutionary”.

Man in Singapore gets protection order against wife who sent AI obscene images
The court found the act of sending of fake images and videos of the man and his sister engaging in sexual acts amounted to family violence
A family court has granted a man a personal protection order (PPO) against his wife, who had abused him emotionally or psychologically with text messages about him having sex with his sister.
The court found that the sending of fake images and videos of the husband and his sister engaging in sexual acts, generated by artificial intelligence, amounted to family violence.
The man had sought the PPO alleging that his wife had inflicted emotional or psychological abuse on him by accusing him of having sex with his sister.
The wife had an acrimonious relationship with her husband’s sister, according to a judgment published on Wednesday.
The man said what sparked the saga was that he had agreed to contribute S$100,000 (US$79,120) towards his father’s medical bills.
He also informed his wife that he had transferred about S$65,000 to his sister.

items.body_text:
Hysan courts fintech office portfolio as ZA Bank commits to new Causeway Bay headquarters
As landlords navigate soft office demand, tech and digital enterprises are stepping in to capitalise on falling rents and more favourable terms
Digital bank ZA Bank is taking 45,000 square feet (4,181 square metres) across four upper floors at Hysan Development’s Lee Garden Eight for its new headquarters, adding to a wave of financial and technology companies reshaping Causeway Bay’s commercial landscape.
The leasing push comes as Causeway Bay and Wan Chai continue to absorb office supply, with demand recovering more slowly than in Central. Grade A office vacancy in the two districts stood at 9.8 per cent in August, according to property consultancy JLL.
Hysan’s office portfolio was 93 per cent occupied at the end of June, down from 94 per cent six months earlier. Office turnover fell 1.3 per cent in the first half to HK$694 million (US$88.5 million), while rental reversions remained negative, according to interim results published in August.
“The new economy tenant portfolio is becoming stronger,” said Ricky Lui, Hysan’s executive director and chief operating officer. Leasing activity, he noted, had picked up recently, with the current tenant mix roughly split among financial services, professional services and co-working operators.

items.body_text:
您即將進入之新聞內容 需滿18歲 方可瀏覽。
健康網》週末一覺睡12小時小心傷腎！ 醫揭「黃金補眠3法」
〔健康頻道／綜合報導〕假日爆睡是補眠還是傷腎？一名35歲工程師平日經常加班到深夜，週末動輒睡超過12小時，健康檢查卻發現尿蛋白異常、腎功能指數下降。洪永祥診所院長洪永祥指出，長時間睡眠不一定代表身體獲得充分休息，反而應注意是否存在睡眠品質不佳、睡眠呼吸中止或其他健康問題，別把「一直想睡」單純當成補眠。他同步分享黃金護腎補眠4原則。
洪永祥於臉書發文分享，3 5歲的工程師阿傑平日加班到深夜，週末最愛「補眠」，動輒一覺睡超過12 個小時。他以為這樣能修復身體，直到健康檢查發現尿蛋白轉為陽性，腎絲球過濾率（eGFR）從 95 驟降到72而慌張就醫。事實上，假日爆睡，多數人可能以為補眠，卻造成一邊讓腎臟缺水，一邊忽視昏睡的真正病因。
黃金護腎睡眠時間是6到8小時
洪永祥說明，國際權威期刊《Sleep Health》與《American Journal of Kidney Diseases （AJKD）》的多項大型追蹤研究顯示，睡眠與腎功能呈「U 型曲線」：每日睡眠少於6小時或超過9小時的人，慢性腎臟病（CKD）與蛋白尿風險顯著增加14%至20%。
他接著說，「爆睡」往往是病徵，而非原因，文獻明確提到，超長睡眠常常是睡眠品質極差或慢性發炎的表現，缺氧加上超長睡眠，對腎臟的傷害絲毫不輸給熬夜。最黃金的護腎睡眠時間，其實是6到8小時。
假日爆睡為什麼傷腎？洪永祥表示，連續十幾個小時不上廁所也不喝水，身體持續流失水分，血液濃縮會使腎臟血流量驟降，過濾廢物的負擔瞬間暴增。尤其，平日睡太少、週末暴睡會強烈干擾生物鐘，降低胰島素敏感性，誘發慢性發炎與高血壓，這正是腎衰竭的兩大幕後黑手。
洪永祥建議補眠護腎黃金3法則，補眠不超過 1 小時，假日固定時間起床，避免打亂生物鐘；醒來先喝水，床邊放杯溫水，起床立刻補充 200c.c. 稀釋黏稠血液；查明長睡原因，若總是睡不飽、響鼾連天，應盡快檢查是否有睡眠缺氧問題。

items.title: 中華信評看好台灣AI供應鏈 信用品質維持穩健
items.summary: 根據中華信評最新發布的「台灣企業2026年信用焦點」報告，台灣科技硬體業者憑藉在AI硬體供應鏈與半導體產業的領先地位，受惠於全球AI基礎設施投資榮景，展現強勁成長動能。中...…
items.body_text:
中華信評今發布台灣企業信用焦點更新報告。（資料照，記者吳欣恬攝）
〔記者吳欣恬／台北報導〕根據中華信評最新發布的「台灣企業2026年信用焦點」報告，台灣科技硬體業者憑藉在AI硬體供應鏈與半導體產業的領先地位，受惠於全球AI基礎設施投資榮景，展現強勁成長動能。中華信評指出，台灣高度整合的AI硬體與半導體生態系，有助於企業全面享受AI需求爆發帶來的成長紅利，且受評企業普遍維持審慎的財務管理，整體信用品質維持穩健。
中華信評首席分析師許智清指出，過去三年受評台灣科技業的應用市場經歷重大轉變，AI基礎設施已取代個人電腦（PC）與智慧型手機等傳統終端設備，成為最大的營收來源。隨著五大雲端服務供應商持續擴大資本支出，2026年至2027年雲端業務與AI基礎設施營收將是帶動台灣科技公司成長的核心關鍵。
報告顯示，台灣企業在關鍵AI硬體市場中占有極高市占率，其中先進晶片代工與雲端/AI伺服器領域市占率均超過90%，電源與冷卻解決方案及IC載板亦占有30%至60%的比重。市場領導業者如台積電、鴻海、台Delta（台達電）與欣興電子等，因在AI基礎設施供應鏈中擁有強健地位，其獲利能力與EBITDA利潤率均獲得顯著支撐。
中華信評表示，雖然為了滿足以美國客戶為首的需求，業者在分散產能與營運資金上的資本支出有所增加，但強勁的EBITDA成長與穩定的自由營運現金流量，使受評企業的借款槓桿比（借款對EBITDA比）維持在低水準。相較於亞太區與北美同業，台灣受評科技硬體發行體在財務管理上相對保守審慎。
針對市場擔憂AI投資可能放緩的風險，中華信評進行情境壓力測試顯示，即使在「雲端/AI營收較基本情境下滑50%、EBITDA利潤率下降30%」的極端假設下，受評企業的合併EBITDA仍可維持在接近2025年的水準，資本報酬率亦足以保持在相對於評等為允當或正向的水準。中華信評認為，因AI波動性而導致負向評等行動的可能性相當有限，台灣科技業評等擁有充裕的財務緩衝空間。

items.title: 中華信評示警 台灣化學品業獲利與信用前景承壓
items.summary: 受中國長期產能過剩、地緣政治不確定性及貿易壁壘影響，台灣大宗化學品業的獲利能力與信用前景持續面臨下行壓力。中華信評最新發布的信用焦點報告指出，雖然2026年上半年產業出現...…
items.body_text:
中華信評今發布台灣企業信用焦點更新報告。（資料照，記者吳欣恬攝）
〔記者吳欣恬／台北報導〕受中國長期產能過剩、地緣政治不確定性及貿易壁壘影響，台灣大宗化學品業的獲利能力與信用前景持續面臨下行壓力。中華信評最新發布的信用焦點報告指出，雖然2026年上半年產業出現局部復甦，但整體績效表現恐將持續低於景氣循環週期中期的水準，多家受評化學品企業的評等展望已呈現負向或列入信用觀察負向。
中華信評資深高級分析師賴冠伃表示，荷姆茲海峽局勢的不穩定，是2026年全球貿易與能源價格的最大不確定因素。加上亞太區乙烯平均產能利用率在經歷長時間的下行週期後，2026年可能進一步下探。
報告分析，隨著化學品供應鏈波動劇烈推升價格，加上企業前期取得的低成本庫存逐步耗盡，預計2026年下半年業者的利潤率空間將受到擠壓。此外，主要市場持續建構貿易壁壘，亦對大宗化學品業者的出口活動與獲利復甦造成干擾。
中華信評統計，目前的「負向」評等展望主要集中在大宗化學品與金屬等高景氣循環性產業。包括台塑企業四大公司（台塑、台塑化、台化、南亞）評等展望均為負向；台灣聚合化學品與亞洲聚合亦被列入「信用觀察負向」。
中華信評指出，產品差異化與成本優勢將決定各化學品業者的復甦速度。像是大宗通用化學品，如台聚等業者，由於產品組合中產能過剩的芳香化合物與乙烯占比較高，受到的競爭與價格壓力最為沉重。
在多元與特用化學品的部分，長春集團因特用化學品業務貢獻占比高，得以維持較佳的獲利表現；台塑集團則可透過煉油、電子材料與特用化學品的業務分散性，逐步支持其獲利能力恢復。奇美實業雖產品集中度較高，但憑藉淨現金部位與正向的現金流量產生能力，能為信用評等提供些許緩衝空間。

items.body_text:
New Zealand deployed two naval vessels to monitor North Korea’s illicit maritime activities from mid-August to early September, Japan’s foreign ministry announced after the ships concluded their sanctions enforcement mission.
The Royal New Zealand Navy frigate HMNZS Te Mana and sustainment vessel HMNZS Aotearoa conducted surveillance in waters surrounding Japan, the ministry said in a press release Tuesday, marking the third time New Zealand naval vessels have carried out such activity since 2024.
The mission focused on “illicit maritime activities, including ship-to-ship transfers with North Korean-flagged vessels,” which are prohibited under U.N. Security Council resolutions, according to the ministry.

items.title: Battery demand surges in North Korea as customs clearance opens
items.summary: North Korean trading companies are placing sharply higher orders for batteries now that customs clearance has opened between China and North Korea, but strict safety procedures for the fire-prone cargo mean supply still cannot keep pace with demand. North Korean trading companies have significantly increased their orders for batteries of all kinds in recent weeks, […]
items.body_text:
North Korean trading companies are placing sharply higher orders for batteries now that customs clearance has opened between China and North Korea, but strict safety procedures for the fire-prone cargo mean supply still cannot keep pace with demand.
North Korean trading companies have significantly increased their orders for batteries of all kinds in recent weeks, including small and midsize batteries in the 12 to 30 amp-hour range, commonly used in electric bicycles and motorcycles, a source in China said Thursday. Demand has grown alongside the rising popularity of electric bicycles and motorcycles inside North Korea, but has also increased with the number of households and businesses seeking to store solar power.
“Batteries make up a fairly large share of the orders these days,” the source said. “It is not just for electric bicycles and motorcycles, either. A lot of people also want to store solar power at home, so demand keeps climbing.”
In a country where the electrical grid remains unreliable, small and midsize batteries have become essential household items. They power not only transportation but also lighting, LCD televisions and small electronics, according to the source.
Pent-up demand surfaces as trade channels open
Authorities limited official customs clearance for batteries for years, making it hard for North Korean buyers to secure the volume they needed. That changed recently when formal clearance became available to traders, and the backlog of unmet demand is now surfacing all at once, the source explained.
“After the problem of putting food on the table, electricity is what every North Korean covets most,” the source said. “Batteries let people store electricity and use it when they need it. Naturally, a lot of people are eager to get their hands on them.”
Even with official trade channels now open, batteries cannot simply flow freely across the border. The batteries can catch fire from impact or overheating during storage and transport, so Chinese authorities classify them as hazardous cargo, requiring stricter customs procedures than ordinary goods.
A battery awaiting shipment to North Korea recently exploded at a bonded warehouse at China’s Dandong customs house, a border crossing point that handles a large share of China-North Korea trade, the source said. “A battery caught fire while waiting to be shipped out this past July,” the source said. “There have been similar incidents before, both big and small. That is why officials scrutinize batteries more closely than other goods.”
As a result, batteries from multiple North Korean trading companies are now pooled together to reach a set volume. Officials then clear the pooled batteries as a single shipment, rather than sending them out individually as orders come in.
“You cannot just order a few batteries and load them onto any truck,” the source said. “Orders have to be pooled together to build up volume. Traders also have to complete the necessary procedures before customs will clear them, so it is hard to fill individual orders right away.”
The opening of official customs channels has allowed North Korean battery orders to climb quickly, but the cargo’s hazardous classification and the demanding clearance process mean rising demand has not translated into a smooth expansion of supply.
Electric bicycles and motorcycles continue to grow more popular inside North Korea, and more households are also turning to solar panels paired with storage batteries to generate their own electricity. Both trends suggest demand for batteries will remain strong for the foreseeable future.

items.title: Satellite imagery shows reservoir drought worsening across North Korea
items.summary: I analyzed satellite imagery from the European Space Agency’s Sentinel satellites throughout August 2026. My goal was to assess the condition of major agricultural reservoirs across North and South Korea. The review found that a summer heat wave and abnormal weather patterns have driven a sharp, widespread reservoir drought. Optical images from the Sentinel-2 satellite […]
items.body_text:
I analyzed satellite imagery from the European Space Agency’s Sentinel satellites throughout August 2026. My goal was to assess the condition of major agricultural reservoirs across North and South Korea. The review found that a summer heat wave and abnormal weather patterns have driven a sharp, widespread reservoir drought. Optical images from the Sentinel-2 satellite showed a clear pattern across three reservoirs supplying North Korea’s grain-producing regions. Each lost more than 17% of its water surface area compared with last year. The affected sites, the Sangjwa Reservoir, the Chongsan Reservoir and the Muan Reservoir, all showed broad stretches of dry lakebed exposed along their edges.
Radar imagery from the cloud-penetrating Sentinel-1 satellite told a similar story south of the border. South Korea’s Jangsong Lake, a critical water source for the Honam plain in South Jeolla province, suffered an even steeper decline. Its surface area shrank by 43.4% over the same twelve-month period. This drought on both sides of the border arrives just as rice enters its critical ripening stage. The timing raises serious concerns about the size of this fall’s harvest. North Korea appears especially vulnerable in this regard, since its aging and poorly maintained irrigation systems leave crops with little buffer against water shortages.
North Korean reservoirs show sharp declines
My analysis of Sentinel-2B and Sentinel-2C optical images focused on reservoirs feeding North Korea’s western grain belt. These reservoirs lost significant water surface area over the past year. The losses stem from the ongoing heat wave and unusual weather patterns affecting the region. The Sangjwa Reservoir, located in Jangyon county, South Hwanghae province, shrank from 76 hectares to 59 hectares, a decline of 22.4%. That retreat, equal to 17 hectares, left large sections of exposed lakebed visible along its margins. The Chongsan Reservoir, in Jeungsan county, South Pyongan province, followed a similar trajectory, contracting from 112 hectares to 93 hectares. That 17% reduction left wide mudflats visible around the reservoir’s perimeter.
Declines of this magnitude, occurring at the same point in the growing season as the previous year, point to serious drought conditions in these areas. August marks the period when rice grains fill out and ripen, and it is also when agricultural water demand peaks across the country. Low reservoir levels during this critical maturation window raise the likelihood of reduced yields when North Korea’s fall harvest arrives.
Localized rain swells one North Korean reservoir amid the wider drought
Not every reservoir I examined in this review showed a decline this summer. The Muan Reservoir, in Liwon county, South Hamgyong province, shrank from 32 hectares to 25 hectares, a drop of 21.9%. Its banks grew noticeably narrower, and its water level dropped in visibly obvious fashion. Bongrae Lake, in Pyonggang county, Kangwon province, moved in the opposite direction. Its surface expanded from 517 hectares to 603 hectares, an increase of 16.6%, pushing outward toward the lake’s outer edges. I also noted that the lake’s water had turned an emerald and murky shade. That change is consistent with an inflow of sediment and debris from heavy localized rainfall. Taken together, these opposing trends indicate that eastern North Korea experienced both drought and concentrated heavy rain within the same short window. The pattern underscores how unevenly this summer’s abnormal weather has struck different parts of the country.
South Korea’s Jangsong Lake reveals an even steeper decline
Jangsong Lake is a large reservoir in South Jeolla province. It supplies agricultural water to Jangsong county, Gwangju, Hampyong county and Naju. Of every reservoir in my review, it showed by far the most severe drought effects. items.title: In North Korea, a Chinese phone now costs as much as a house
items.summary: Chinese phone prices have surged along North Korea’s border with China this year. Intensifying crackdowns and a halt in state-led smuggling have sharply reduced the number of devices reaching the region. A source in Hyesan told Daily NK on Friday that Chinese phone prices in the city have jumped by more than 10,000 yuan, or […]
items.body_text:
Chinese phone prices have surged along North Korea’s border with China this year. Intensifying crackdowns and a halt in state-led smuggling have sharply reduced the number of devices reaching the region.
A source in Hyesan told Daily NK on Friday that Chinese phone prices in the city have jumped by more than 10,000 yuan, or roughly $1,489, in recent months. The devices have become so scarce that buyers now pay a steep premium just to find one for sale.
Chinese phones in Hyesan are now trading for at least 35,000 yuan, or about $5,212, with some models selling for even more, the source said. The devices previously sold for between 25,000 and 30,000 yuan, or roughly $3,722 to $4,467, depending on the model. Prices climbed further once the available supply began to tighten.
Along the border, remittance brokers and prominent cash brokers rely heavily on Chinese phones. The devices are their main link to counterparts across the border. North Korean authorities regard Chinese phones as a major channel for leaked internal information and incoming outside news. Enforcement against Chinese phone users has steadily intensified as a result.
In January 2026, the National Intelligence Agency, formerly the Ministry of State Security, ordered its border-area intelligence departments, formerly known as state security departments, to carry out so-called mopping-up operations against Chinese phone owners and users. Field offices were instructed to establish so-called clean zones free of the devices by the end of the year.
Chinese phone prices climb as smuggling routes narrow
Crackdowns on Chinese phone users have continued since January. The source said a narrowing of the smuggling routes used to bring devices into the country has further pushed up prices.
North Korea’s pandemic-era border closures effectively cut off individual smuggling operations, leaving state-led smuggling as the main channel for Chinese phones entering the country. That channel has grown increasingly difficult to use as well, the source said. As a result, the flow of devices into North Korean markets has shrunk further.
Despite the crackdown, demand for Chinese phones inside North Korea has not let up. Some buyers need a replacement after their existing phone breaks down. Others discard their devices to destroy evidence when they fear being caught, which creates fresh demand for new units.
The source put the scale of the price increase in blunt terms. “No matter how much money you have or how much you earn, a minimum price of 35,000 yuan is going to be a burden,” the source said. “That amount could buy a single-story house in downtown Hyesan.”
The source also described why traders keep buying despite the cost. “For people trading with China, a Chinese phone is basically a moneymaking tool,” the source said. “No matter how expensive they get, people who need one to keep earning money have no choice but to buy one, however reluctantly.”
Rising prices reshape how devices are shared
The price surge is also changing how Chinese phone users along the border share their devices. In the past, users who fell behind on their bills or needed a temporary replacement would sometimes borrow a phone from someone in the same line of work. That practice has become far less common, the source said. Losing a borrowed phone now means absorbing a costly loss.
“The phones are so expensive right now, and the risk of getting caught is so high, that people almost never ask to borrow someone else’s phone anymore,” the source said.
Remittance brokers have grown more selective as well, the source said. They now weigh a counterpart’s reliability, the amount involved and the level of risk before accepting a job. That is a shift from taking on every request as they once did.

items.title: Hollands opens up on axing from Carlton AFL roster
items.summary: Elijah Hollands is at peace with the end of his Carlton career, saying he realises there are more important things in life that he needs to focus on.
items.body_text:
In short:
Carlton has delisted seven players from its AFL roster.
One of those delisted was Elijah Hollands, months after suffering an on-field mental health episode.
Hollands took to social media after being delisted, thanking the greater AFL community for its support since his mental health challenges became public.
Elijah Hollands is at peace with the end of his Carlton career, saying he realises there are more important things in life that he needs to focus on.
Hollands was one of seven players delisted by the Blues on Wednesday, with former GWS star Zac Williams, Jordan Boyd, Lachie Fogarty, Lewis Young, Flynn Young and Harry Charleson also among the casualties.
But it was Hollands' axing just months after suffering an on-field mental health episode that represented the biggest story.
Carlton was fined $75,000 for its handling of Hollands during a round-six loss to Collingwood.
Hollands tallied just one disposal for the match, with his erratic behaviour catching the attention of fans even before the game started.
The 24-year-old was hospitalised days later before deciding to step away from football to concentrate on his mental health.
It meant Hollands wasn't able to add to his 47-game AFL career, 14 of which were played at Gold Coast.
His brother Oliver Hollands remains at Carlton.
Elijah took to Instagram to share his thoughts about the end of his time at the Blues, which could also spell an end to his AFL career.
"Football means an extreme amount to me," Hollands wrote.
"My dad played professional footy, my great-grandfather played professional footy, my brother plays professional footy — it is everything I have lived and breathed for as long as I can remember.
"I have only ever wanted to do one thing my entire life: copy what was done before me and play AFL footy. It was something that I just knew I was going to do when I was a kid and it was all I ever cared about.
"And now, unfortunately, that purpose I had is no longer.
"I love this game, but I have come to realise that there are things in my life that are far more important than footy right now and they're the things I will now prioritise."
Hollands thanked the greater AFL community for its support since his mental health challenges became public.
"As an extremely confident 18-year-old, I certainly envisioned my career going a whole lot differently, but I am OK with accepting that it just isn't in the plans set for me," Hollands said.
"I'll be moving into the next chapter of my life, leaving what will feel like a big hole to fill, but I am excited about what can come from having my health and mind in much greater shape."
Carlton's other big delisting was Williams, who joined the Blues from GWS at the end of 2020 on a six-year deal believed to be worth about $5 million.
The soon-to-be 32-year-old managed only nine games this year, with his time at Carlton plagued by injuries.
AAP
